> **Windows desktop control.** The model sees the real screen and drives the real
> mouse and keyboard.

Out of the box, a DeepSeek Harness session can reason about your desktop but cannot
touch it: you describe what is on screen, you take the screenshots, you do the
clicking, and you report what happened. **dsh-pilot closes that loop.** The model
looks at the real pixels and then operates them:

| tool | what it does |
| --- | --- |

## Why this exists

A model that cannot see the screen has to be told what is on it. A model that cannot
touch the screen has to be told what to do next. That turns every desktop task into a
conversation about the desktop instead of work on the desktop — and the user becomes
the hands, the eyes, and the error message.

The expensive part of desktop automation was never the mouse. It is **how many times
the model and the computer have to talk**:

| a five-step task: focus a window, click a field, type, press Enter, look at the result | DSH alone | DSH + dsh-pilot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| who reads the screen | you | the model, from real pixels |
| who clicks and types | you | the model |
| model ↔ computer round trips | 5 (one per step, plus yours) | **1** |
| screenshots shipped to the model | 4–5 | **1** |
| where the model spends its time | waiting, re-describing, re-asking | thinking about the task |
| when a step fails | you notice | the same result says which step, and why |

## What it feels like

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as You
    participant M as Model
    participant P as dsh-pilot
    participant W as Warm worker (PowerShell)
    participant D as Your desktop
    U->>M: 把第三列改名成 Q3 收入并保存
    M->>P: screen_view(window: "报表")
    P->>D: capture (per-monitor DPI aware)
    D-->>M: real PNG + cursor, foreground window, monitor bounds
    M->>P: desktop_sequence([focus, click, type, key, key])
    P->>W: 5 requests over one pipe — 6–12 ms each
    W->>D: SetCursorPos, SendInput, clipboard paste
    D-->>M: one end frame (with coordinate rulers) + per-step outcome
```

## Why the coordinates can be trusted

The classic way a vision-driven click goes wrong is a coordinate that is *almost*
right. dsh-pilot removes the three ways that happens:

**1. Both halves are per-monitor DPI aware.** A DPI-unaware process is lied to by
Windows: it sees a 2560×1600 panel as 1707×1067, so every click computed from such a
screenshot lands in the wrong place. The sensor and the effector each declare
`SetProcessDpiAwarenessContext(PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2)` before doing anything, so one
image pixel is one physical screen pixel.

**2. Frames carry rulers.** Ticks every 200 px along the top and left edge, each
labelled with the **screen coordinate** it sits at, plus an `origin x,y step n` note.
The model reads a position off the image instead of counting pixels — and because the
labels are screen coordinates, they survive any downscaling the attachment store does.

**3. The envelope says what it actually delivered.** If the store re-encodes a frame
smaller, the model is told the ratio and the multiplier, and the coordinate contract
becomes conditional — it only promises "use x and y as they are" when the delivered
frame *is* the capture:

```text
<image_size delivered="1974x873" captured="2261x1000">1974x873</image_size>
<delivered_scale>delivered 1974x873 = 0.873x capture; multiply image readings by 1.1454 to get screen pixels</delivered_scale>
```

## Why it is fast

Batching is the big win (round trips, not clicks). The second win is that PowerShell
stops being restarted: one warm worker process answers every action and every frame.

| request | one-shot script | warm worker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| action (`move`, `click`, `type`, …) | ~0.9–2.0 s | **6–12 ms** |
| capture (primary monitor) | ~1.2–2.3 s | **~0.5 s** |

Measured on a 2560×1600 panel at 150% scaling with the harness UI animating. The
worker is started in the background on the first tool call, so the ~1 s it needs
overlaps the first capture instead of delaying the first action.

**Identical frames are not resent.** Every capture returns a `frameHash`; when a frame
is byte-identical to the previous one of the same session, the image is not attached
(or stored) again — the result says `unchanged: true` and the coordinates from the
frame the model already has still apply. `forceImage: true` overrides it.

## Reading the control tree

A screenshot costs a guess: the model finds a button in pixels, estimates its centre,
clicks, and takes another frame to see whether the guess was right. Windows exposes the
same control through UI Automation as a role, a name and a rectangle, so the click
becomes the centre of that rectangle and nothing has to be looked at.

```js
desktop_control({ action: 'controls', title: 'Notepad' })
// 4  [Button] '最小化' @ 887,1 45x39
// 14 [Button] '新建会话' @ 12,54 256x24
// 23 [Edit]   '搜索会话名称' @ 204,238 4x20  offscreen

desktop_control({ action: 'click', target: 14, title: 'Notepad' })
```

**The tree is not a faster screenshot; it is a different trade.**

| | screenshot | control tree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one read | ~150 ms, ~1k tokens | ~130-300 ms, ~850 tokens (filtered) |
| click target | estimated from pixels | the control's exact rectangle |
| state | "looks disabled" | `enabled`, `offscreen`, `HasKeyboardFocus`, `IsSelected`, value |
| availability | always | **not always** - see below |

Per call the tree is slower or level. Per task it is much faster, because one read
resolves several targets without another frame and without another round trip.

**It does not always exist.** A canvas, a drawing surface, a custom-painted list and an
Electron window that publishes nothing all give an empty or useless tree. That is why
the screenshot path is still there and still the fallback: read the tree first, take a
frame when the tree is empty or when you need to see what is drawn rather than what is
declared.

**Three things worth knowing.**

- An index addresses one row of one listing. It is resolved against a fresh read at
  click time, and the worker remembers the listing it handed out, so a row that changed
  identity fails loudly instead of being clicked by position:
  `the control at index 4 is not the one that was listed: expected [Button] 'OK', found [Button] 'Cancel'`.
- `meaningfulOnly` (default `true`) returns only the roles a person can operate. On a
  real 673-element window that is 77 elements and ~850 tokens instead of 9k - the rest
  is layout panes with no name, no state and nothing to click. Pass `false` for the
  whole tree.
- `includeValues` is off by default: structure is not content. Password fields are
  masked even when it is on.

**When the thing you want has no tree of its own** - a chat transcript, a canvas, a
custom-painted panel - do not look for it. Look for what surrounds it and subtract: the
composer is an `Edit` with a rectangle, the window has a rectangle, so the transcript is
what is left between them. Or skip the geometry: select the item in the tree, confirm
with `HasKeyboardFocus` that the keyboard is where you want it, type, press Enter. That
last step is something a screenshot cannot do - it can show a caret, not a promise.

## Why it is safe

Giving a model hands is the part worth getting right:

- **Risk is declared, then enforced.** Low risk (default) batches freely. A batch
  declared `medium`/`high`, or one carrying a step marked `risk: "high"`, is refused
  *before anything touches the desktop* unless the caller passes `confirm: true` —
  which it does only after you agreed.
- **`dryRun: true`** validates a batch and lists the plan without executing.
- **Stop on the first failure** (default): a refused `focus` can never be followed by
  typing into whatever window happens to be in front.
- **Targeted input.** When a step names a window (`hwnd`), the effector re-asserts it
  as foreground immediately before injecting, so a click cannot land in a neighbour.
- **An unknown outcome is never a silent retry.** If the worker dies after a request
  was delivered, the action is reported as failed rather than repeated — it may
  already have taken effect. A capture has no side effects, so it *is* retried.
- **Interruption works.** Pressing Esc writes a cancel token, the action loop polls it
  between every step (during drags, during the settle wait, before the capture) and a
  drag releases the button in a `finally` block, so an aborted turn cannot leave the
  mouse latched down or the remaining clicks playing out.
- **It cannot lie about privilege.** Windows refuses input injection into a
  higher-integrity (elevated) window; the tool reports that failure instead of
  pretending it worked.
- **`desktop_sequence` is bounded** by `maxSequenceSteps` (default 24).

- **The request pipeline resizes again after capture**, and this plugin never saw
  that step: on a 2560x1600 display the frame reached the model as 1610x1006 while
  the contract said "delivered at capture size … do not rescale", so every reading
  taken off it was 1.59x off. The contract now **predicts** the projected size from
  the image budget the deployment publishes, and prints the size and the multiplier:
  `2560x1600 capture -> 1609x1006 preview, multiply every reading by 1.5911`. A frame
  whose area fits the budget arrives untouched, so framing the window or a region
  gives a true 1:1 frame — 1365x960 does, 1024x768 does, 4K and 5K say 2.2642x and

  elements at 0.3 s on the next call. A caller that trusts the first answer concludes
  the window has no tree and falls back to pixels for nothing. `controls` now retries
  once, 300 ms later, when the worker has not yet seen a real tree and the answer is
  suspiciously small.
- **A filtered listing that legitimately matches nothing** now says so, instead of
  returning an empty list that reads as "this window has no tree":
  `(no operable controls here; the window has 2 elements - pass meaningfulOnly:false to see them)`.

- **`controls` reads the window's UI Automation tree**, and `target` clicks a listed
  control's exact rectangle, so a named control no longer has to be found in pixels.
  It takes no screenshot, so it pays no settle. Measured on a 673-element window:
  **0.65 s** and **~850 tokens** filtered (77 operable elements) against ~9k
  unfiltered. The worker remembers the listing it handed out, so an index whose row
  changed identity fails instead of clicking whatever took its place.
- **The settle was paid even when nothing was captured** (0.5.9). It exists so a frame
  is not taken mid-repaint; `desktop_control` applied it on every call, capturing or
  not. Measured **814 ms -> 12 ms** for a non-capturing action.
- **A refused `focus` was reported as success** (0.5.9). The step recorded a note, said
  `ok`, and the rest of the batch went to whichever window was actually in front. It
  now checks the foreground window after the attempt — the state, not
  `SetForegroundWindow`'s return value — and fails, naming both. `tolerant: true`
  restores the old behaviour for a caller whose coordinates are right either way.
- **The peer range now accepts the 0.2.1 host generation** (0.5.10). The 0.2.1 tuple
  needed its own prerelease comparator: a prerelease only satisfies a range when a
  comparator carries a prerelease tag on the same `major.minor.patch`.

**0.5.8** — two fixes, and the package is now on npm as
[`@momasiku/dsh-pilot`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@momasiku/dsh-pilot).

- **The monitor geometry could go stale, and silently.** The inventory came from
  `System.Windows.Forms.Screen.AllScreens`, a static cache that only refreshes
  when the process pumps `WM_DISPLAYCHANGE`. The warm worker is a
  `-NonInteractive` read loop with no message pump, so nothing ever invalidated
  it. Measured: a worker alive 13 hours reported
  `<screens>primary WinDisc 0,0,1600,900</screens>` while the same result carried
  `<image_size>1024x768</image_size>` — two answers to one question, inside the
  very frame the coordinate contract is read from. Monitors now come from
  `EnumDisplayMonitors` per capture and the virtual screen from
  `GetSystemMetrics`; neither caches.
- **The cold start paid for the bridge every time.** The Win32 bridge was compiled
  with `Add-Type` on every process start, before the worker could answer
  `ready` — exactly the cost the warm worker exists to stop paying twice. It now
  compiles once into a DLL keyed by a hash of its source, then loads that.
  One-shot capture **2638 ms → 813 ms**; warm actions unchanged at **9 ms**. A
  source edit changes the hash and therefore the DLL, so a stale cache can never
  shadow a later fix.

The npm name is scoped because `dsh-pilot` on npm belongs to an unrelated
browser-automation plugin. **The repository is still `momasiku/dsh-pilot`.**

## Tools

### `screen_view`

| parameter | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `screen` | string | `primary` (default), `all` (whole virtual desktop), or a 0-based monitor index |
| `window` | string | case-insensitive substring of a window title or process name; frames that window |
| `region` | string | crop as `x,y,width,height` in physical screen pixels |
| `includeCursor` | boolean | draw a crosshair at the pointer (default `true`) |
| `rulers` | boolean | draw the coordinate rulers (default: the `rulers` setting) |
| `forceImage` | boolean | attach the frame even when it repeats the previous frame of the session |

The result carries the image plus a `<screen_capture>` envelope: delivered size,
capture size when they differ, physical origin, scale, every monitor's bounds, cursor
position, and the foreground window (title, process, class, bounds) — then the
coordinate contract for that frame.

### `desktop_control`

| parameter | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string, required | `click`, `doubleClick`, `rightClick`, `middleClick`, `move`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, `focus`, `windows`, `controls` |
| `x`, `y` | integer | target in physical screen pixels; required by the pointer actions and by scroll-at-a-point |
| `toX`, `toY` | integer | drag end point, or a nonzero value to make `scroll` horizontal |
| `text` | string | text to insert for `type` |
| `key` | string | a character, `enter`/`tab`/`esc`/`f5`, or a chord like `ctrl+s`, `alt+tab`, `win` |
| `amount` | integer | wheel notches for `scroll` (default 3, positive scrolls up) |
| `button` | string | `left` (default), `right`, `middle` |
| `title` | string | window title or process substring; required by `focus`, filters `windows` |
| `hwnd` | string | lock input to one window handle (`0x1094C` or decimal) |
| `capture` | boolean | capture a fresh frame after acting (default `true`) |
| `settleMs` | integer | wait before that capture so the screen can repaint (default 750) |
| `forceImage` | boolean | attach the frame even when it repeats the previous frame of the session |
| `target` | integer | pointer actions: click the control at this index from a `controls` listing instead of `x`/`y` |
| `includeValues` | boolean | `controls`: also return each control's value (default `false`; passwords masked) |
| `meaningfulOnly` | boolean | `controls`: only operable roles (default `true`) |
| `tolerant` | boolean | `focus`: record a note instead of failing when Windows refuses the foreground |

`type` delivers text as **one paste** (clipboard set, `Ctrl+V`, clipboard restored), so
applications see a single insertion — multi-line text and CJK included — instead of a
burst of per-character keystrokes. `windows` returns every visible titled top-level
window with its bounds, minimized state, and which is foreground: useful before
clicking anything.

`controls` returns the window's control tree as one line per control — `index [Role]
'Name' @ left,top widthxheight` plus `disabled`/`offscreen`/`value` — and takes no
screenshot (pass `capture: true` if you want one anyway). Feed an index back as
`target` to click that control's exact centre. See **Reading the control tree** above
for when a tree exists and when a frame is still the right tool.

### `desktop_sequence`

| parameter | type | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | array, required | ordered steps; each is one `desktop_control` action **without** its own screenshot, plus optional `settleMs`, `risk`, `riskNote`; action `wait` takes `ms` |
| `risk` | string | `low` (default) / `medium` / `high` — the risk you declare for the whole batch |
| `confirm` | boolean | required for a medium/high batch; without it the tool refuses before touching the desktop |
| `dryRun` | boolean | validate the batch and list the plan without executing anything |
| `capture` | string | `end` (default) captures one frame after the last step, `none` skips it |
| `target` | string | `window` (default: the window that was foreground during the batch), `screen`, or `all` |
| `window` | string | frame this window instead (title/process substring), overriding `target` |
| `region` | string | crop the end frame as `x,y,width,height` in physical pixels |
| `forceImage` | boolean | attach the end frame even when it repeats the previous frame |
| `stopOnError` | boolean | stop at the first failing step (default `true`) |
| `settleMs` | integer | delay before the end capture so the screen can repaint |

Every step comes back with its own action, duration in milliseconds, and outcome — so
one call still tells the model exactly where a batch went wrong.

## Settings

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: pilot
      name: dsh-pilot
      config:
        captureRetention: 30   # frames kept under .dsh-pilot/
        timeoutMs: 20000       # per-call kill deadline for a helper
        settleMs: 750          # default delay before the automatic capture
        stepSettleMs: 120      # per-step delay inside a desktop_sequence
        maxSequenceSteps: 24   # hard cap on the steps of one batch
        alwaysSaveFile: true   # keep the PNG even when no image block is attached
        useWorker: true        # keep one PowerShell process warm (6-12 ms actions)
        rulers: true           # draw coordinate rulers on every frame
```

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph JS["lib/index.js (the plugin)"]
        T1[screen_view] --> C[capture]
        T2[desktop_control] --> A[runAction]
        T3[desktop_sequence] --> A
        C --> R[frame hash + dedup + envelope]
    end
    C -->|warm request| W[desktop-worker.ps1]
    A -->|warm request| W
    C -.->|fallback| PB[desktop-probe.ps1]
    A -.->|fallback| AB[desktop-action.ps1]
    W --> WC["_dsh-win32.ps1 · _dsh-action.ps1 · _dsh-capture.ps1"]
    PB --> WC
    AB --> WC
```

Two halves, one coordinate space: the sensor reports the geometry, the effector
consumes the same physical pixels, and `GetCursorPos`/`SetCursorPos` report back, so
the loop is self-checking.

The shared code sits in `_dsh-win32.ps1` (the Win32 bridge and DPI awareness,
idempotent), `_dsh-action.ps1` (`Invoke-DshAction`) and `_dsh-capture.ps1`
(`Invoke-DshCapture`). The one-shot scripts stay as thin bootstraps — they are what
the plugin falls back to when the worker cannot be used. The worker speaks one
base64 JSON request per line, answers with one JSON line per request, and keeps
serving after a failed action, a failed capture, or a cancelled step.

Captured frames land in `<session cwd>/.dsh-pilot/` and are pruned to
`captureRetention`. Pruning never breaks an image the conversation already carries,
because attachments are stored content-addressed.

## Troubleshooting

| symptom | cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `no visible top-level window matches "..."` | the window is hidden to the tray or the title changed; `desktop_control { action: "windows" }` lists what is really there, and `hwnd` targets a window that has no title match |
| clicks land next to the target | the frame was delivered smaller than the capture — check `<delivered_scale>` and apply the multiplier |
| a click does nothing | the target window may be elevated; Windows refuses input injection across integrity levels |
| the tools are missing after an update | restart the desktop app: a package's code is re-imported on load, and the profile's plugin rows are composed at boot |
| a batch refuses to run | it was declared `medium`/`high` (or contains a `risk: "high"` step): re-send with `confirm: true` after the user agreed, or `dryRun: true` to see the plan |

## Developing

The smoke tests load the plugin against the real `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` from the
desktop checkout, so they exercise every schema and renderer without a harness restart:

```powershell
# the package resolves @deepseek-ai/* from the desktop app's node_modules
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path node_modules\@deepseek-ai `
  -Target "D:\AGAENT\DSH Desktop\resources\app\node_modules\@deepseek-ai"

node tools/smoke.mjs          "D:\AGAENT\DSH Desktop\resources\app"  # load, schemas, renderers
node tools/render-smoke.mjs   "D:\AGAENT\DSH Desktop\resources\app"  # coordinates: 1:1 vs shrunk, contract, rulers
node tools/sequence-smoke.mjs "D:\AGAENT\DSH Desktop\resources\app"  # end-to-end batch on a throwaway window
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\script-smoke.ps1  # PowerShell half + worker protocol
```

`sequence-smoke.mjs` drives a real batch against a throwaway window it creates
itself (never one of your applications) and the window writes back what it received —
so "focus, then type, then Enter" is proven to have happened **in that order**, not
merely attempted. `script-smoke.ps1` drives the PowerShell half directly: the one-shot
paths, the worker handshake, warm latency, a failing action, a cancellation, a failing
capture, and that the worker survives each of them. The last two need a full-access
shell: the plugin reads its helpers through pipes, which a restricted sandbox denies
with `EPERM`.

The helper scripts can be driven by hand while debugging — they take a UTF-8 JSON
params file and print one JSON result:

```powershell
'{"out":"E:\tmp\shot.png","screen":"primary","rulers":true}' | Set-Content params.json -Encoding utf8
powershell -NoProfile -File lib\scripts\desktop-probe.ps1  -ParamsPath params.json
powershell -NoProfile -File lib\scripts\desktop-action.ps1 -ParamsPath params.json
```

Keep the `.ps1` files saved **with a UTF-8 BOM**: Windows PowerShell reads BOM-less
files as ANSI, which mangles non-ASCII window titles and paths.

### Reinstalling after an edit

`dsh plugin add file:...` installs a **copy**, and a repeat `add` of an unchanged
`file:` spec reports "Already up to date" without re-copying even when the files on
disk changed. After editing, copy the changed files into the installed package
yourself and restart the desktop app:

```powershell
$src = "E:\path\to\dsh-pilot"
$dst = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\<profile>\node_modules\dsh-pilot"
Copy-Item "$src\lib\index.js" "$dst\lib\index.js" -Force
```

### Why the smoke test validates result shapes

A tool result carrying a key its closed output schema does not declare is rejected by
the runtime **after** `execute()` has already performed the side effect — so the action
happens yet the caller sees an error. A schema-only check cannot see that failure
mode, so `smoke.mjs` validates a realistic result object against each tool's compiled
output schema, and additionally asserts that the validator itself catches the
undeclared `ok`/`actedAt` keys that shipped once.

# dsh-unlag（解除卡顿）

**DSH 桌面端、网页端自己的刷新按钮。**

开发插件要重启，可手里还有任务在跑？刷新一下！
开久了页面越来越卡？刷新一下！

一个按钮解决这些烦恼，正在进行的会话不受影响。窗口右上角点一下：插件代码原地换掉，卡顿的界面重建一次，宿主自己的轮次、子代理、终端进程继续跑完。

桌面 App 的窗口里有它，`dsh web` 打开的浏览器页面里也有。两边认得出来是哪个：桌面壳会把自己的桥交出来，网页没有这座桥。

## 两个日常场景

| 情况 | 按一下 |
| --- | --- |
| 改了界面类插件，手里还有任务在跑 | 插件当场换掉，宿主自己的任务继续跑完 |
| 界面越用越卡 | 直接恢复流畅，会话、队列、草稿都还在 |

以前两种都得关掉 App 再来。现在不用，也不用挑空闲时间——马上换，不等。

边界说清楚：宿主自己的轮次、子代理、终端进程不受影响；被换掉的那个插件如果自己负责某个正在跑的任务（例如 agent-loop），这个任务会随实例结束。主脚本以外的资源不能配对时，会保留当前页面并说明原因，不会硬重建。

## 装

```sh
dsh plugin install dsh-unlag
```

安装后由 DSH 完成首次加载，之后的更新都走按钮。

## 用

点右上角那个按钮。右键菜单有三行，另有一项在配置里：

- **按下刷新时换掉插件代码**（默认开）
- **按下刷新时重建界面**（默认开）
- **Agent 可以自己刷新**（默认关）

前两行都开＝先换代码再重建；只开一个＝另一项完全不动；都不开＝点击无反应。最后一行只决定谁能按，不改变按下去做什么。

「改完文件自动刷新」不是菜单行，是配置项（默认关），开了也不用按按钮。

页面自己缺插件时会主动说一句：应用在两次启动之间换过插件代码，新开的页面按启动时那份冻结清单去要脚本会答 404，那个插件就没加载，屏幕上原本什么都不会说。现在页面启动后读一次开机时记下的应答，只有应用明确答「这个地址没了」时，才在按钮旁说「缺插件，重启应用后恢复」——不用按任何东西。读不到、读不全或清单太长时保持安静。这句话不是某次刷新的结论，所以不会到点消失，按下一次后由新的结果接替。

插件换过之后，页面按旧版本号要的懒加载分块，只要这个文件还在就按它现在的版本答：文件还在、只是编号变了，不该算缺插件，也不该让人只剩重启。文件真没了才拒绝并点名是哪个文件。

## 谁能让它刷新

默认只有人：自动刷新关着，Agent 入口也关着，本插件不装任何文件监视，本插件自己永远不会去换代码。

右键按钮里打开「Agent 可以自己刷新」后，会话里的 Agent 可以自己按这个按钮（工具名 `unlag_refresh`），复用按钮那套判定与拦截，但只换宿主侧的插件代码：页面不会重开，也不会替你按下按钮；内容没保存、插件没恢复时照样停住并说明原因。关着时 Agent 调它会被告知先打开开关，不会偷偷刷新。还有子任务（subagent）在跑时，Agent 调它会被拒绝并列出这些子任务：换插件会把子任务插件一起换掉，在跑的子任务会被中止；等它们结束再刷新，或由你自己按按钮。

这不等于 App 自己也不会换：宿主自带的插件热更新有自己的开关和监视，装了开发插件、开着那边的自动应用时，改文件仍可能由宿主应用；本插件开关关掉只是本插件不发起。

## 不会丢什么

- 正在跑的轮次、子代理、终端进程：宿主进程不重启，会话记录和排队消息都留着。被换掉的插件实例会先关掉：如果某个正在跑的任务由那个插件自己负责（例如 agent-loop），这个任务会随实例结束；宿主自己的轮次不受影响。
- 界面重建会重新进入同一个地址：屏幕上正在显示的内容重新载入一次，会话记录还在。
- 排队消息：排在宿主里，重建文档不影响它。
- 输入草稿：重建前先提交焦点里的内容，文字草稿由 App 自己存下来，回到同一会话还在。
- 附件：草稿里的附件只存在当前页面里，文字草稿会存下来，附件不会。草稿里确实还有没发出去的附件时，按钮会停住并说明先发出去；消息发出后留在记录里的图片不算草稿，不会挡住刷新。
- 有未保存改动、开着弹窗、或下个页面要用的模块读不全：拦下并提示，提示里写明卡在哪一项，宁可不刷。
- 原来就起不来的插件不挡换代码，但也算不算「可以重建」：启动以来就没跑过的插件只记日志；上一次更新打坏、还没恢复的必要插件，会在结果里点名，并且下一次按也不会被当成已修好。
- 四个开关读不到时不硬刷：提示稍后再试，日志记下是哪一步没读到，绝不谎称代码已是最新。
- 旧页面记着的启动清单分组变了（装过／卸过插件）：按插件逐个补齐再交给新页面，不会因为清单 404 把 App 带走。
- 从不自己重启或退出 App。

管不到（它会拦下并说明，不会硬来）：

- 改动替插件加原生能力、改服务声明或权限：这类改动不在一次点击的范围里。
- 独立进程和进程级的东西：宠物窗口自己的配置、DSH 自身升级、原生依赖变化。
- 万一新页面还是起不来：App 会进入错误恢复（退出，或请你停用第三方插件）。本插件不替你选，也不会自己重启或退出 App。

## 依据的官方约定

- 页面启动时，宿主把插件清单写成 `window.__DSH_BOOT__`；脚本地址形如 `/plugins/??<包>/client.js&rev=<修订>`，修订由文件的修改时间、变更时间、大小决定（`docs/subsystems/client-modules.md`）。
- 宿主对未知、被改过、过期的修订返回 404，不会拿别的字节顶上，也不会让单页应用的回退把 HTML 当脚本发出去（同上）。
- 插件代码重建、但入口没重启时，宿主用 `rebuilt()` 发布新修订，页面按新地址只换掉那一个插件（同上）。
- 页面只应用自己启动时那一版宿主的清单；宿主换了版本，页面要重新载入才能跟上（同上，Host release changes）。

本插件只做这些约定允许的事：换代码走宿主的插件重载入口，重建走一次页面载入。唯一的差异在下一节。

## 与官方约定的差异

官方的插件资源路由对未知修订返回 404。本插件对旧页面记着的旧修订返回当前内容：桌面版在窗口启动时固定了启动清单，页面按旧修订请求脚本是常态，返回 404 会让新页面起不来、App 直接退出。这是本插件的兼容措施，不是官方行为。右键按钮里的开关只决定按下去做什么（换插件代码／重建页面／自动刷新／允许 Agent 按），关掉开关不会停掉这套兼容措施。

同一原因下的第二种情况：启动清单里记着的插件在配置里已经被关掉或删掉了，官方路由对那一行只会 404。本插件改为返回一段空脚本，让这一行不再 404；那个插件因此不会被加载，页面是否能起来仍取决于其余启动行和官方启动流程。日志会写明哪个插件被留下，`/dsh-unlag/verify` 的结论里也带 `leftOut` 字段。

## 排错

- 日志：`~/.dsh/unlag-reload.log`，换代码／跳过／被拦各一行，含原因。
- 演练：`npm run smoke` 不按按钮，只按当前启动清单把下一个文档要加载的字节在沙箱里跑一遍，看每个插件是否都注册（`rehearsal.ok`），并当场核对三件事：写死的旧版本号仍然拿得到现在的字节（`shim.staleRev`），按下前会做的那个判断此刻是否放行（`pressPath`），以及那个判断本身会不会误拒（`verify.sound` 应为 `ok`、`verify.broken` 应为 `blocked`、`verify.refuses` 与 `verify.accepts` 为 `true`）——它证明的是「启动清单里的每个插件都注册了、每个分块都取得到、按钮此刻真的可按、拦住的是坏清单」，不换任何代码；演练里的 Loader 只收集注册的 ID，不执行插件的 factory、import 与 apply，所以它不等于整机刷新已经安全。
- 同一支脚本还现场核对路由的守门规则（`contract`）：读路由只认读、写路由缺 `x-dsh-unlag` 头或来自别的源一律 403、未知路径 404。它用的是和页面一样的请求，所以这条规则在运行中的 App 上是否还在，一眼可见。
- 状态：`GET /dsh-unlag/state` → `{"version":"<当前版本>","code":"<index.js 写入时间>","plugins":true,"page":true,"shim":{...},"served":{"status":"served|missing|unknown","entries":<当前插件图行数>,"id":"dsh-unlag"}}`。`code` 用来分清「版本号没刷」和「旧代码真的还在跑」；`served` 用来分清「按钮没出现」是插件图里没这一行（`missing`）、还是图还没就绪（`unknown`）。
- 重建后的日志带起页面代次：`interface rebuilt; the page runs the plugins as served now (page <rev>)`，据此判断新文档加载的是新脚本还是旧脚本。
- 按钮不出现且 `served` 是 `missing`：先看 profile 的 `package.json` 里 `dsh.profile.bundles` 还列不列着 `dsh-unlag`。宿主装别的插件时会按 `dependencies` 重算这份有序清单，手装或软链进来的条目可能被一并丢掉，加回去、重启即可。装清单失败与插件本身无关，已提上游：。
- 装不上、报 `ECONNREFUSED` 或 `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`：先看 `~/.npmrc` 里的代理是否在跑，代理没起时换镜像直连也能装。

每类说法对应的测试与现场输出整理在 [EVIDENCE.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-unlag/blob/HEAD/EVIDENCE.md)，含还没证到的两件事。

## 与官方文档的对照

判定按下后能不能重建，依赖的是 Client Modules 的读接口和它自己公布的路由规则。逐条核对的是 App 内随包发布的文档 `.research/asar-dsh/dsh-client-modules/README.zh.md`（15968 B，sha256 前缀 `33cee13e7b61a151`）。

| 官方规则（该文档行） | 这里的做法 | 为什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 未知资源或 revision 返回 404（80） | 冻结的启动清单里的行，旧 revision 照样给现在的字节；表里已经没有的插件仍然 404 | 桌面壳从启动时读到的清单重启文档，任何一行 404 都会让壳以退出码 1 结束，正在跑的会话随之死掉。只在「这一行确实还在表里」时接管，别的 404 原样放行 |
| 启动图与批次 URL 是应用目录相对形式（80） | 校验时按同样形式（`plugins/??…&rev=…`）读，相对路径补前导 `/` 后再取 | 与文档一致，避免把文档相对形式当绝对路径 |
| 每个阶段在 URL 超过 3 KiB 前分区（80） | 一行超过 8 KiB 就拒检（`blocked/list`） | 官方既然在 3 KiB 前分区，真实启动行就短于 3 KiB（这台机器实测最长 2834 B），8 KiB 只挡伪造清单，不会误拒正常行 |
| revision 由 mtime/ctime/大小派生，不哈希内容（80、136） | 只用官方读接口拿到的 revision，不自己算版本；比对的是正文里注册的插件 id | 哈希会引入一套自己的代际，和官方的 404 规则打架 |
| bundle 内容变更只能通过 `rebuilt()` 进入图（78） | 不调用 `rebuilt()` | 调了会让运行中的页面就地换模块，草稿和正在跑的任务受影响；这里只换宿主侧代码，页面由人来按按钮重开 |
| 图更新在同一个 Loader 上串行执行（90） | 重建走宿主自己的插件重载，不自己改 Loader | 自己改会和官方协调逻辑冲突，这是不能碰的那层 |

## 改完后让运行中的 App 用上

不用重启 App，也不用重启页面：换掉 `index.js` 后让插件的记录重载一次即可。

1. 改版本号，并 `touch index.js client.js`。**只改版本号是不够的**：插件的装载按文件时间判断要不要重新读，时间没变就还是旧代码在跑，`/state` 里会看到版本号没变（或变了但 `code` 是旧的）。
2. 在插件列表里把本插件关掉再打开。这两步之后 `~/.dsh/unlag-reload.log` 会出现一行新的 `dsh-unlag <版本>`。
3. 等约 20 秒，读 `GET /dsh-unlag/state`：`version` 是新版本、`code` 是刚才 `index.js` 的写入时间，才算真的换上了。
4. `npm run smoke` 对着运行中的 App 复核一遍（见下一节）。
5. 发布用 `./scripts/release.sh`，它发完会回查 registry 是否真的列出版本。`npm view` 读的是 CDN 缓存，发布成功后的一两分钟里可能还显示上一版；`npm view` 与 registry 不一致时，以版本号文档（`https://registry.npmjs.org/dsh-unlag/<版本>`）是否 200 为准。

页面那一半（按钮点击后的重建）不在这一步里：那是按钮本人的事，只有人能按。

## 测试

```sh
npm test
```

对着正在运行的 App 走一遍真实判定（页面半、宿主半都是线上代码，用的是 App 现在渲染的启动清单；只回答「能不能刷」，绝不按按钮），并核对路由契约：读接口 200、写方法 405、不带页面头的按键路由 403：

```sh
npm run smoke
```

没有 App 在监听时打印 `skip` 并退出 0。

2119143833890537478.desc: 会话头一个按钮停掉回合、目标和后台任务，写盘；重启后同一个按钮把工作接回来。
2119143833890537478.content:
# dsh-pause-resume

One button in the DeepSeek Harness session header. It stops what is running — asking a running turn
to wrap up first — writes a small plan to disk, and after a restart the same button puts that work
back.

* ⏸ — work is running. Press to stop it.
* ▶ — work is stopped, or a previous process left work to restore. Press to restore it.
* ↻ — a turn stopped on its own. Press to continue what did not finish.
* ⏸ dimmed — nothing to stop, restore or continue.

The glyph is the only status. There is no counter, no panel, no badge and no toast, because a second
indicator would be a second source of truth for the same fact. When the last press left something for
a person to look at, the one-sentence tooltip says so and the button still offers the same glyph.

## What it restores

| Work | Pause | Restore |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A session with an unfinished turn | turn wrapped up or cancelled, session recorded | session mounted, then one visible continuation message |
| A goal that was armed | paused with the revision it had | `goals.resume` with that exact revision; the goal driver continues on its own |
| A session that only carried that goal | recorded, nothing stopped | mounted; the resumed goal takes over |
| A running background job | killed and recorded | recorded only: a job is a live process, not replayable, so the continuation message names it and the turn restarts it if the work still needs it |
| A session that ended normally | untouched | untouched, and never recorded in the first place |
| A terminal / finished session | untouched | untouched |
| A schedule | untouched | untouched |

Schedules are not paused: the schedule service has no disable operation, only delete, and deleting a
person's schedule to pause it is not a trade this plugin makes. A schedule that fires while paused
starts a turn, but the button keeps showing ▶ while a pause plan waits: a pending plan owns the main
action, so the only honest next step is to finish the restore. The schedule appears in that restore
summary like any other work started after the press.

## What a pause does

A press does not cancel at once. It first asks the turn that is running to wrap up, and cancels only
what is still running when the window closes: `wrapUpMs` (default 3000; `0` cancels immediately, as
every version before 0.9.0 did). A turn that ends inside the window is stopped as completed; the rest
are cancelled when the time is up, so a pause still never leaves a turn running behind it. Either way
the plan is written and the sessions are recorded, and the next step is the same: press ▶ to restore,
or restart and let the plan be picked up. When something had to be cancelled, the tooltip says the
work to continue is saved; when everything wrapped up by itself, it says nothing extra.

If the window closes with the steer still unread, the press takes it back: a pause that did not happen
must not replay later as a fresh instruction in the restored session. Only that one message is
removed, only for sessions that timed out, and only while it is still queued; when the queue is not
readable the report says `retractUnavailable` instead of claiming a clean queue.

A plan nobody will press again closes itself. After a restart by hand, finishing those sessions
yourself is enough: each stopped turn is seen living on, moved forward and no longer running, so the
plan settles the way a completed restore does and the button returns to pause, with no press. Only
turns the pause itself stopped are considered, and only on positive evidence: a session still working,
a session list that cannot be read, or an error keeps the plan exactly as it was.

## How resume works

A restore is not a claim that work continued. It is three honest steps per item:

1. **Mount.** A stopped session is mounted through the Harness resume path, which preserves its agent
   preset. If it is already mounted, that step is skipped.
2. **Continue, only where the press actually cancelled a turn.** The continuation is one ordinary
   user message sent through `sessionController.prompt`, with a request id derived from the plan and
   the session. The id makes a repeated restore idempotent, and the message is visible in the
   transcript, so the person can see exactly what was resumed.
3. **Re-arm a goal** with the revision it had when paused. The revision is the person's veto: if the
   goal changed while paused, it is not ours to resume and the item is `skipped`.

Every attempt is journaled with the id of the process that made it, but a journal is reporting, not a
promise: the next boot asks the live Harness again instead of trusting an old row. The continuation
request id is derived from the plan and the session, so a retry before a turn starts is deduplicated
by the Host. A failure leaves the plan on disk and the next press retries every item that still needs
work.

A subagent session cannot be mounted by this process: its parent chat owns the routing. That row is
reported once as attention for the parent, not retried as a failure, so it never keeps the plan open.

## Crash, not just a press

A press writes a snapshot. A crash writes nothing, so the plugin keeps a heartbeat instead:
`running.json` holds the sessions whose turn is open right now and the id of the process that wrote
it. The previous process's record is turned into a crash plan in `pending.json` before the heartbeat
file is replaced, so a second or third restart still sees the same work and offers ▶ with no press
needed.

A crash record is weaker than a press: it proves a session existed, not that a turn was open after the
restart. Restore attaches every recorded session and reads the live turn. A row whose turn is still
running is continued; a row that is idle is left idle by the probe, which mounts it to read it and does
not prompt it. A row whose state cannot be read or proven is reported as unknown, and unknown is not
finished: the plan stays on disk, the button keeps offering ▶, and the next press tries again. A
recorded goal is restored whether or not its session's turn is provable, because dropping it was the
path that ended a crashed set with every goal in attention and none resumed. Sessions that ended
normally never enter the file.

The same process reloading the plugin (hot reload) sees its own id and knows there is nothing to
restore. A `pausing` plan found on disk means the press itself was interrupted: those sessions are
left alone, and the button keeps offering the restore until a person presses it.

## Stops that were not a press

A turn can end without a person pressing anything: the provider returns an error after its own
retries, or the model hits its output limit. Those turns are the one case a restart cannot fix on its
own, so the plugin keeps a separate small ledger, `continue.json`, and offers ↻ instead of ▶. The
ledger is independent of the pause plan: it never turns into a crash plan, never pauses or cancels
anything, and never sends a message by itself.

What becomes a candidate:

* A session's latest turn ended `error` or `max-tokens`, and no later turn started or ended.
* The session is a root session with no parent and is not a subagent. A child's stop is answered by
  its parent's tool result; continuing the child alone would speak into a conversation nobody reads.
* The turn did not end `completed`, `aborted`, `interrupted` or `blocked`. A manual pause aborts its
  turn, so the stop a person asked for never appears here; a block before admission is work that
  never ran and is left alone.

The press continues the rows visible at that moment, two at a time, with an ordinary user message.
It is not a retry loop: a row that fails stays in the ledger for the next press, and the button
returns to ↻ when anything is still waiting. A row disappears when a newer turn starts, when the
session is already open, when the goal is active, when the session is gone, or when the continued
turn completes. Title comes from the session's own title event; nothing is loaded just to name a
row. The batch is capped at 40 rows, and a row keeps its attempt number across failed presses.

Each row is labelled for display only: `blocking` when it already needs a person or its error code is
one a retry cannot fix (auth, permission, quota, unknown model, context length), `actionable` otherwise.
`pendingContinue` carries both counts next to `count`, so failed work stays visible while a batch is
running; the label never hides a row and never changes what a press does — one press still continues
every visible row.

Starting a new message in a session that has a waiting row is a takeover: it clears that row without
claiming anything about the old work. Work continues only after a press, never on plugin load, never
on a timer, and never because the previous batch failed.

## Progressive restore (off by default)

Six long sessions restored at once are six upstream model requests at once, and a gateway that is
happy with one slow stream is often unhappy with six. For Direct API users this is usually fine and
the extra waiting is pure cost, so progressive restore is **off by default**: restore follows the
ordinary path with no added spacing, no request pool and no cooldown timer installed at all.

Turn it on when batch restores run into rate limits or timeouts: a shared account or gateway quota,
a self-hosted proxy with limited capacity, or an environment where restoring several sessions at
once is what triggers the failures. Single-session timeouts are not helped by it; those need
investigation of the request and the upstream.

Two layers, because either alone is enough to defeat the other:

* **Dispatch spacing.** Sessions are restored in waves by lineage depth, with a gap of
  `restoreStartGapMs` (3 s) plus up to 0.4 s jitter between starts.
* **A real request pool.** The plugin registers an `llm/stream` middleware and holds one permit per
  adapter request until that stream ends, fails or is cancelled — not when the turn opens, not when
  the first chunk arrives, and not when a tool or subagent wait begins (that request is over).
  Compaction enters the same pool with `purpose: 'compaction'`, and every official retry takes a
  fresh permit. The guard is open only while a restore runs, so ordinary chatting is never queued
  behind it.

The pool starts at `restoreCapacity` (1). Two clean streams in a row raise it by one, up to
`restoreMaxCapacity` (2). Two failures in a row drop it back to one and close the pool for
`restoreCooldownMs` (40 s), so one unwell upstream cannot be hammered by a queue of sessions. An
abandoned stream (the person paused) is neither a success nor a strike: cancelling is cheap.

The switch is read when you press restore; a running batch keeps the setting it started with, so
turning the feature off mid-batch cannot suddenly release the queue. Press pause to stop the
current batch.

Nothing about reliability depends on this switch. Pause and restore of sessions, subagents and
background jobs, pausing again during a restore, plan persistence, crash recovery, continuation
deduplication and the retry entry all still apply with progressive restore off. The restore loop
keeps its own small worker waves either way; only the extra limit on real model requests is
optional.

Pausing while a restore is running is immediate. The press stops dispatching, refuses every request
still waiting for a permit, asks the Harness to stop the work that already started, writes what is
left back to the plan as an outstanding continuation, and returns `paused` with
`interrupted: true`. The next press resumes the same plan; the continuation request id is per cycle,
so a message already admitted is deduplicated instead of sent twice.

`/state` reports the setting and the queue while a plan exists: `{progressive, active, enabled,
capacity, running, queued, dispatched, failed, interrupted, cooldownUntil}` under `restore`. The
button itself stays icon-only.

Configuration (all optional):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `restoreProgressive` | `false` | opt-in staged restore; off keeps the plain path |
| `restoreCapacity` | `1` | model requests allowed when a restore starts |
| `restoreMaxCapacity` | `2` | ceiling the health gate may raise the limit to |
| `restoreCooldownMs` | `40000` | pause after two consecutive failures across sessions |
| `restoreStartGapMs` | `3000` | spacing between restore starts, plus jitter |
| `wrapUpMs` | `3000` | how long a running turn has to wrap up before a pause cancels it |

Scope, stated honestly: this governs requests that pass through this Host's model stack. The
Harness's own restore flow and a subagent that reaches a provider outside this Host are outside the
pool, and no plugin can promise a concurrency limit for a company gateway it does not own. The
300 s upstream idle timeout is an upstream decision; progressive restore cannot pretend to fix it,
but it makes the restore produce evidence (one session, one exact request) instead of an avalanche.

## Restore pacing and heap headroom

Restoring a session deserialises its whole transcript into the Host heap. One large session is
GB-scale on its own, and the Host's V8 has roughly a 4 GB ceiling; past it the process does not
throw, it dies with `FATAL ERROR: MarkCompactCollector: young object promotion failed`. Measured
twice on 2026-10-29: pid 91126 after 64 minutes at 3.65 GB, and pid 61989 fifteen minutes after
restoring 15 sessions at 3.58 GB. Both left `crash-*-host.log` under
`~/Library/Logs/DeepSeek Harness/`.

So a restore is paced by what it can afford to hold, not only by what it has to do:

* **Only what this crash interrupted.** Sessions recorded by the crash plan are restored; history
  and sessions that ended normally are never touched. That is unchanged since 0.6.x.
* **Smallest first.** The queue is ordered by transcript size, so light sessions go first and heavy
  ones last. Light sessions run `restoreConcurrency` (2) at a time.
* **Heavy sessions run alone.** A session whose compressed transcript is above `restoreHeavyMB`
  gets a step of its own; the next one starts when its turn ends, or after `restoreSettleMs` (90 s)
  as the upper bound.
* **One press drains the queue.** A row held back only because an earlier restored session was
  still working is retried by the engine itself, one `restoreSettleMs` later, until nothing is left.
  Before 0.8.4 the same press mounted exactly one large transcript and left the rest for a person to
  press for again, which is what `partial` after every restart looked like. The retry stops on a
  stop the person asked for, on a reload, and after `restoreMaxAttempts` rounds that restored
  nothing.
* **Heap gate.** Before each step the restore reads `v8.getHeapStatistics()`. If the headroom left
  is below `restoreHeapReserveMB`, the round mounts nothing further. A session that did not get its
  turn is recorded in `deferred` and left unstarted — loading its transcript is exactly the cost the
  gate exists to avoid — and the next press or the next boot picks it up.
* **Predicted before mounted.** Admission also estimates the heap a transcript will take (six times
  its compressed size) and holds the row back when the estimate does not fit the headroom that is
  left, so a huge session is refused before it is read rather than after it has grown the heap. A
  session whose size cannot be read is treated as heavy and goes through the serial heavy path;
  `/state.scheduling.unknownWeights` reports how many this round could not measure.

A round that held rows back does not consume the plan: it ends `partial`, keeps every row on disk
with its `deferred` note, and `/state.restore.deferred` lists what it could not mount. Consuming it
would have deleted the only record of work that had never started, and the next boot would offer a
clean restore while a large session was still owed.

When a round restored a heavy session or produced `deferred`, `/state` also carries
`restartRecommended` with the heap usage and the reason, and the client's tooltip switches to
"重启后继续没放下的内容" once rows are waiting on a restart. The plugin never exits or restarts the Host itself: a process
is a person's running work, and a plugin that killed it for a cleaner heap would be paying with
data it does not own.

The advice lives as long as the work it is about: it is kept while `/state.scheduling.deferred`
lists rows that this round held back (the next press cannot mount them either), it is cleared by a
healthy round with nothing deferred, and a recommendation from more than six hours ago is dropped
unless rows are still waiting. A row that was held back keeps the intention it had (mount or
continue) and comes back with it on the next restore.

The three memory numbers are derived from the heap this Host actually has, not written down here:
a 4 GB V8 cap and a 16 GB one cannot share a reserve, and a small cap wants one session at a time.
`/state.scheduling` reports the resolved values plus `derived`, which says which of them came from
the heap instead of from config.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `restoreConcurrency` | `1` if the V8 cap is under 3 GB, else `2` | light sessions restored at once in one round |
| `restoreHeavyMB` | `heapLimitMB / 340`, clamped to 8–48 MB | compressed-transcript size that makes a session heavy |
| `restoreHeapReserveMB` | `22%` of the V8 cap, clamped to 320–1536 MB | heap headroom below which a round mounts nothing |
| `restoreSettleMs` | `90000` | upper bound to wait for a heavy session's turn |
| `restoreMaxAgeHours` | `72` | a crash record older than this is archived, not mounted |

All four are optional; setting one pins that number and leaves the others derived.

This is a different layer from progressive restore. `restoreProgressive`, `restoreCapacity`,
`restoreMaxCapacity` and `restoreCooldownMs` limit real model requests to the upstream; these four
limit how much transcript a restore holds and how many sessions it steps through. Both can be on,
and neither replaces the other. The crash evidence, the scheduling flow and the `deferred` /
`restartRecommended` fields are described in `docs/memory-safety.md`.

## Supported platforms

macOS, Windows and Linux. State and logs go through `node:path` and `node:fs` only, under
`$DSH_HOME` (or `~/.dsh` when the variable is unset); nothing calls a shell and nothing shells out
to `stat`, `du` or `ps`. Cross-process exclusion uses a `session.lock` file rather than POSIX-only
calls. On Windows the directory `fsync` has no equivalent, so it is skipped — a write is still a
temp file plus `rename` — and that, together with line endings, is the only difference between the
platforms.

## Installing

```bash
plugin_manager install_bundle dsh-pause-resume
```

or install the bundle from the Harness plugin manager with the package name. Every configuration
key is optional (see Progressive restore) and the plugin holds no credentials. `allowRemote` exists for a Harness reached from another
machine; local-only is the default.

## Guarantees and limits

* **Exclusive.** The phase lives on the Host and is written before any work starts, so two windows,
  a double press and a tool call cannot overlap. The second caller is told `busy` — except a pause
  during a restore, which interrupts it on the spot instead of refusing: stopping must never be the
  operation that waits.
* **Durable before destructive.** No turn is cancelled until the plan is on disk. A failed write means
  nothing was stopped.
* **Bounded.** A restore that keeps failing stays on disk with its rows named; it does not close as
  if the work were finished. A row that cannot be read is retried once and then either reports real
  progress or retires the plan as `partial` with per-row attention, so the button stops repeating a
  no-op. Sessions continued by hand are restored, never re-sent, and their attention row clears as
  soon as they run. An attempt that overruns its budget is watched a little longer before it is
  called a failure, and a session this plan already restored stays restored even if the Harness
  revives it and moves its turn on a later boot.
* **Idempotent.** The continuation request id is derived from the plan and the session, so a retry
  cannot post the same message twice; a turn that already moved is not continued again, and a turn
  a person already continued is reported `already running` instead of being pressed again. The
  Harness has no compare-and-admit, so a sub-second window remains between the last status read and
  prompt admission; the guards narrow it and the outcome never claims atomicity.
* **Honest.** Unreadable state never reports `paused`. A session deleted by hand, a goal changed by
  hand, a session already running: each is skipped and named in the outcome.
* **No hidden takeover.** There is no public API to detach an agent, so the pause guarantee is
  "turns cancelled, goals paused, jobs killed" — not "the process is frozen". A goal continues because
  the Harness has a mechanism for that; a plain session continues through one visible user message.
* **No third-party plugin state.** A plugin's in-process state belongs to that plugin's mount.
* **Local by default.** The routes require a same-origin request and a plugin header. Remote use must
  be opted into and still cannot skip the header.

## Files

All state lives under `$DSH_HOME/pause-resume/`:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `snapshot.json` | the work a press stopped, `pausing` or `paused` |
| `pending.json` | a crash plan, kept until a restore finishes |
| `journal/<planId>.jsonl` | restore attempts, tagged with the boot that made them |
| `restores/<planId>.json` | the archived plan, kept as a record of the last restore |
| `last-restore.json` | summary of the last restore |
| `running.json` | sessions with an open turn, for crash residue |
| `continue.json` | turns that stopped on their own and wait for one continue press |

Every write is a unique temp file, `fsync`, `rename`, then a directory `fsync`. State is never inside
the package.

## Development

```bash
npm test
npm run audit
npm run smoke:host   # boots a throwaway real Host on a free port and asserts the routes
npm run smoke:live   # real Host + local mock model stream: pause, SIGKILL, restart, resume once
npm run smoke:maintenance  # real Host: pause cancels an in-flight compaction, apart from the session turn
npm run smoke:wrapup # real Host + held model stream: the turn answers the pause as an ordinary completed turn
```

The wrap-up path has its own record in `docs/evidence/host-wrapup.json` (a real turn that ends itself
inside the window, so the plan owes one continuation), next to `docs/evidence/host-live.json` (a
window that expires, where the press takes its own steer back).

Verification records live in `docs/acceptance-0.6.11.md` (current release: repeated failures stay
continuable, a pause truncates a running batch, admission ownership, handoff proof, cold/stale goal
recovery, continue behind the progressive gate, and blocking vs actionable rows, with the proven and
unproven halves kept apart), `docs/acceptance-0.6.10.md` (self-stopped turns and the one continue press), `docs/acceptance-0.6.9.md` (the ten defects from the previous review), `docs/acceptance-0.6.7.md` (a crash press that moved the
button without restarting anything), `docs/acceptance-0.6.6.md` (an `unknown` row a person
continued by hand and finished, child rows honouring the same intents as roots, the race window, and
what is still unverified), `docs/acceptance-0.6.5.md` (0.6.5), `docs/acceptance-0.6.0.md` (0.6.0–0.6.1)
and `docs/evidence/`. The eight-item mapping from the second review to code and proof is
`docs/objective-round2-closure.md`. The job-lifecycle listening design review, including why a job is
never restarted, is `docs/design/job-lifecycle.md`. The memory-safety policy behind the 0.7.0 restore
pacing — why a restore kills a Host, the crash evidence, the scheduling flow and the fields a person
should look at — is `docs/memory-safety.md`.

`lib/engine.js` performs no I/O, `lib/snapshot.js` persists, `lib/probe.js` holds every Harness service
contract (agent identity, goal revision, per-owner jobs, continuation prompts), and `index.js` only
wires them to the web routes. All of them are testable without a Harness: `test/apply.test.mjs` mounts
the plugin against a fake registry.

2119143833890537477.desc: 让东坡肉滚出系统提示：记忆不常驻，命中只给标题，正文读了才进上下文，项目规范还能自己长。
2119143833890537477.content:
# dsh-lite-memory

**全库不常驻：没有命中的轮次不追加记忆内容，命中时最多三条卡片，正文按需读。**
**Nothing resident: a turn that misses adds no memory text; a hit adds at most three cards, bodies read on demand.**

---

## 它是什么 / What it is

给 DeepSeek Harness 的轻量记忆：全库不进常驻提示、不逐轮注入、不扫描文件。记忆只在两种时刻出现——你说「记一下」，或者这句话跟已有条目真有关（最多三条卡片：标题、摘要、前提，正文仍按需读）。

Lightweight memory for the DeepSeek Harness. Nothing resident: no standing prompt, no per-turn injection, no file scanning. Memory appears at exactly two moments: you ask it to remember, or the message genuinely overlaps an existing entry (at most three cards with title, summary and preconditions; bodies are read on demand).

## 触发方式 / Triggers

| 场景 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| **L0** 你明确要求「记住这个」 | 立即写盘，一条确认行 |
| **L1** 它发现有跨会话价值的经验 | 一行灰字 `memory · suggested "X"` + 一个「保留」按钮；标题加一句话，看得懂才点，不点就永远不写，48 小时内不重复 |
| **L2** 常识、一次性参数、凭据的值 | 永不写入 |

这些行只属于产生它的那一轮：每轮按那轮自己的工具结果重建，重进会话还能看见，别的轮不会混进来。再记一次时插件自己判是更新还是新增：同一层里标题（或这条用过的旧标题）完全一致就更新原条目，前置条件不同也更新这一条，不并存两条同名；换过说法而标题变了的旧标题记成别名以后也认得。像但不同名的不写：先在结果里回「相近：X」，确认要更新就用那个标题重存，确认是另一条才加 `resolution="distinct"`——另存要换个能区分的标题。更新时没给的字段保持原值，正文整段替换——旧正文只作内部撤回依据，不展示、不参与检索。旧数据里已经分叉的同名条目，下一次写入这一层时自动收并成一条，另一条进可恢复归档。读取时标题只记得一半（到逗号或括号为止）也认得：唯一一条前缀对得上就直接读，对得上两条就把候选标题列出来，不猜；同名前缀的归档副本不算第二条候选，活条目优先。

写入时分两层：默认只在这个项目生效；用户说「以后所有项目都这样」才进全局层（200 条起提示，硬上限 1000 条），检索时一起查。同一主题在不同前提下用 `when` 区分，各存一条。

写入前先蒸馏：标题是结论，正文只留原则、判断规则和触发条件，不把具体尺寸、字号、层级、颜色或一次性数字记进来；需要这些值时按记忆里的指针查当前代码或文档。单条正文超过 4096 字节会被拒绝，先删细节再存；摘要超长自动截到 60 字。

触发词：`记住`、`记一下`、`上次`、`规范`、`约定`、`路径`、`凭据怎么取`。

真命中看这句话和记忆的标题（含旧标题）、标签、触发词、摘要有没有对得上的词：有就多一行「已有记忆可能相关」，最多三条标题，每条前面标归属（`[global]` 或项目目录名如 `[DSH]`）；没对上就不出现，不改命中计数，正文要 `memory_read` 才读。一条记忆写了触发词，用户说到那个词也算命中。

普通记忆卡片和实验规则共用一份额度：一次最多 3 条、1200 字节，按整条准入，先到先占；自动提示只带标题和摘要，不带正文。实验短规则（正文不超过 240 字且不超过 4 行）直接带正文，更长的只给标题和用途，正文仍要 `memory_read`。

| Case | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| **L0** you ask it to remember | written immediately, one confirmation line |
| **L1** it spots something worth keeping | one muted line `memory · suggested "X" · sug_x` with a single 「保留」 button — readable before you click, nothing written unless you click, at most once per two days |
| **L2** common sense, one-off parameters, credential values | never written |

The automatic hint carries titles and summaries, never bodies. Normal cards and experimental rules share one budget: at most 3 cards / 1200 bytes per request, admitted as whole cards, first come first served. An experimental rule with a body of at most 240 characters and 4 lines is inlined; a longer one gives only its title and purpose, and the body still requires `memory_read`.

Those lines belong to the turn that made them: each turn is rebuilt from its own tool results, so reopening the session shows them again and no other turn leaks in. Saving again updates an entry whenever the title (or one of its earlier titles) matches exactly inside the same layer — different preconditions still update that one entry, never a second entry with the same title. A merely similar title writes nothing first: the result names the closest entry, so the caller either re-saves with that title or adds `resolution="distinct"`, which requires a genuinely different title. An update keeps every field it was not given and replaces the body wholesale; the previous body is kept only for internal undo and never shown or searched. Legacy duplicate titles already on disk fold into one row on the next write to that layer, and the extra row moves to recoverable archive.

Writes land in one of two layers: the current project by default, or the global layer (warns past 200, hard ceiling 1000) when the user says the rule holds for every project. Both layers are searched together, and a `when` field separates the same subject under different preconditions.

Before writing, distill: the title is the conclusion and the body keeps only the principle, decision rule and trigger condition. Concrete dimensions, font sizes, z-index, colors and one-off numbers stay out; the memory points at where to read the current value instead. A body over 4096 bytes is refused, so drop detail before saving; an over-long summary is truncated to 60 characters.

## 点一下就存 / One click, no turn

「保留」是同源直写：不产生消息、不动输入框、不打断当前回复。点完按钮消失，行变成 `memory · kept`。真写过的行尾才有 `✕`，按标题撤销：改过的条目还原成上一版（显示 `restored`），刚建的条目移入归档（显示 `archived`）；条目后来又改过就停下并说明已经变过，不覆盖后来的修改。没变、需要确认、保存失败的行没有撤销。

The 「保留」 button writes straight to disk from the page: no message, no extra model turn, the input box untouched. It disappears and the row becomes `memory · kept` — that is the whole interaction. Only a row that really changed gets the `✕`, and it undoes by title: an edited entry goes back to its previous body (`restored`), a freshly created one moves to the archive (`archived`); if the entry changed again it stops and says so instead of overwriting. Noop, needs-confirmation and failed saves get no undo.

## 每轮引用条 / Per-turn references

每次回复末尾、在「已编辑 N 个文件」下面，按这一轮实际发生的工具结果留几行：`本轮参考 N 条` 和 `本轮更新 N 条`。点开是记忆名，再点一条就地展开当前正文；名字和正文都取当前值——改过名显示新名字，归档的标「已归档」，删掉的显示「已删除」。同一轮同一条只出现一次；没读过也没写过就整段不出现。切换会话不丢，每轮只按自己的工具结果重建。

Each completed turn keeps a few lines under 「已编辑 N 个文件」, built from that turn's own tool results: `本轮参考 N 条` and `本轮更新 N 条`. A line expands to memory names, a name expands to the body as it is now — current title, current body, archived marked, deleted said outright. One row per entry per turn; nothing read or written, nothing shown. Switching conversations keeps them, because each turn is rebuilt from its own tool results only.

## 记忆面板 / Memory panel

会话头的大脑图标打开居中的记忆面板。浮层挂到 `document.body` 上，尺寸按视口算，宿主容器的高度和定位不影响它；点遮罩或右上角关闭。面板自带错误边界：万一渲染出错，浮层里直接显示原因而不是整个面板消失。内容分「记忆」「自进化」「设置」三个页签：前两页只放内容，开关和调参都在「设置」里，不占列表和宫殿的位置。「设置」里是「启用记忆」「自进化」「记住我」三个开关、「启用图谱」「启用记忆宫殿」两个只影响展示的开关（默认关闭，按项目记住）和排序调参；回执与召回提示只在有话说时占面板底部一行。默认看当前项目，也可以切到其他项目或全局层；切过去只读，不回写、不迁移旧格式。

「记忆」页签里，搜索框右侧可以在「列表」「图谱」「宫殿」之间切换；列表、图谱或宫殿占满内容宽度，选中记忆后右侧才出现正文与归属。当前项目里点「修改」可以就地改标题和正文，保存后版本加一；别的项目和全局层只读。图谱按真实数据画，点记忆节点读正文，点标签或主题节点转成搜索，右上角可缩放。宫殿按类型分四间：习惯与规范、方法与经验、资料与入口、其他记录；一次只展开一间，每间每页 24 条，点展品只读正文。宫殿只决定怎么陈列，不改记忆、学习状态和额度。「自进化」页签只作用于当前项目，按「全部 / 候选 / 试用 / 生效 / 暂停」筛选，也能切列表与图谱；详情给出当前经验、适用范围、当前状态、学习依据和变化记录。候选可采纳、修改、放弃，试用可采纳、修改、暂停，生效可修改、暂停，暂停可恢复或查看记录。

「记忆」页签里另有一张「记住我」卡片，默认关闭，和项目记忆、自进化各自独立。开启后只累计表达偏好：先给结论还是先讲背景、讲多细、要不要举例、语气、选项怎么给等八个维度；技术方案、业务判断、参数、权限、发不发这类决定不在其中。卡片头写已记住几条，已形成的每条标出依据条数，点开能逐条看来源（你明确说过 / 多次选择 / 手动改）并删掉单条；删到没依据就退回观察中。观察中的维度可以直接点「不用这个」，之后同类证据不再累计。关掉只停止继续记，不动已记住的，也不补记关闭期间的对话；「清空画像」只清偏好，不动记忆。

「记忆」页签顶部出现「N 条保存没确认」时，一条保存相近结论的草稿在等决定。先露两条，点「查看全部 N 条」看完整队列；展开给存到哪层、什么时候用、条件、范围清单、触发词、相近条目和完整正文，底部只做「另存」或「忽略」两个动作，不在面板里合并。

The Memories tab also holds a Remember me card, off by default and independent of project memory and self-evolution. When on it accumulates expression preferences only — conclusion first or background first, how much detail, whether to use examples, tone, how options are presented, across eight dimensions; technical approach, business judgment, parameters, permissions and send-or-not decisions are never included. The card header states how many preferences are remembered; each formed one shows its evidence count and can be expanded to see every item (something you said, a repeated choice, a manual edit) and delete a single item. Removing the last piece of evidence drops it back to observing. Any observing dimension can be dismissed with Not this, which stops that kind of evidence from accumulating. Turning the switch off only stops collection: nothing learned is deleted, and conversations from the off period are never backfilled. Clear profile removes preferences and leaves memories untouched.

The brain icon in the session header opens a centered memory panel. Memory and Self-evolution sit at the top, and Display settings at the top right add two presentation-only switches, Graph and Memory palace, both off by default and remembered per project. Two tabs, Memories and Self-evolution, hold the content. When the Memories tab shows “N saves awaiting confirmation”, a draft that resembles an existing note needs a decision. Two rows show first; View all N opens the full queue. Expanding a row shows its target layer, when it applies, conditions, scope list, triggers, similar notes and full body, and the only actions are Save as new or Ignore — the panel never merges on its own. It starts on the current project and can switch to another project or the global layer; switched scopes are read-only and never migrate or create state.

On the Memories tab, the search row switches between list, graph and palace; either view fills the content width, and the body pane only appears after a memory is selected. In the current project, Edit changes a memory's title and body in place and bumps its revision on save; other projects and the global layer stay read-only. The graph is drawn from real data: a memory node opens its body, a tag or topic hub becomes a search, and the top-right controls zoom it. The palace sorts memories into four rooms by kind: Habits and conventions, Methods and experience, References and entries, and Other notes; one room opens at a time, each page holds 24 items, and an exhibit only opens its body. The palace changes presentation only, never memory, learning state or quota. The Self-evolution tab acts on the current project only, filters by All / Candidate / Trial / Active / Paused, and also offers list and graph views. It shows the current rule, scope, state, evidence and change history. Candidates can be adopted, edited or discarded; trials can be adopted, edited or paused; active rules can be edited or paused; paused rules can be resumed or inspected.

- 关闭项目记忆后，这个项目不再使用任何记忆（包括全局层）：自动注入、检索、读取、引用、保存全部停，服务端也拒绝记忆工具和面板修改动作。自进化同时关闭并禁用；重新打开记忆后自进化仍为关闭，要单独开启。
- 关闭只改权限，不删数据：候选、试用、生效、证据、整理额度和默认绑定都保留，计数照常显示。
- 记忆工具与面板管理动作都在服务端拒绝，不能靠改前端绕过；其他项目不受影响。
- 范围只来自服务端枚举的层；不接受客户端拼路径，也不能写别的项目。
- 图谱只按数据画：每条有效记忆一个节点，共享标签和主题做枢纽，显式关联画实线；自进化图谱只连共用条件。位置由条目自身算出来，同一批数据每次一样。

- Turning project memory off stops all memory use in that project, including the global layer: no injection, search, read, citation or save, and the server rejects both memory tools and panel mutations. Self-evolution turns off with it; after memory is reopened, self-evolution stays off until switched on.
- Closing is a permission change, not deletion: candidates, trials, active rules, evidence, organize quota and default bindings are kept, and counts stay visible.
- Memory tools and panel management actions are rejected server-side, so a modified client cannot bypass the switch; other projects are unaffected.
- Scopes come only from the server-side list; the page cannot assemble a path or write another project's notes.
- The graph is data only: one node per active memory, shared tags and topics as hubs, explicit links as solid edges; positions derive from each entry, so the same data looks the same every time.

## 为什么轻 / Why it stays light

- **0 依赖**，存储层无定时器、无监听、无网络，只有同步单文件写；写入用一把有超时的锁，别的进程正在写就明确报「忙」，不抢别人的锁。
- 搜索最多 4 条、400 字；正文只在 `memory_read` 里出现，全文永不进上下文。
- 普通检索只列当前有效的记录；已经归档或被更新替换的旧说法不混进来，要查历史得在 `memory_search` 里显式要 `history`。
- 上限：单条正文 4096 字节、整库正文 1 MB、每层 1000 条、标题与摘要各 60 字；每层 200 条只当提示线。90 天未用只留标题与版本。到了硬上限不拒绝新记忆：把同层最久没被读的一条移进归档，用户固定过的规则不动，保存结果里写明是哪条（正文与完整记录都留着，可人工取回），单条本身超预算才报错；用户明确说「别记」也进归档。文件从不删除。
- 一个项目一个目录，项目之间互相看不见。

- **Zero dependencies.** The store has no timers, no listeners, no network — just synchronous single-file writes, guarded by a lock that gives up after 500 ms instead of stealing it.
- Search returns at most 4 hits and 400 characters. Full text only appears in `memory_read`.
- Normal search lists current entries only; archived notes and superseded wording stay out unless `memory_search` asks for `history`.
- Limits: 4096 bytes per body, 1 MB of bodies per store, 1000 entries per layer, 60 characters per title or summary; 200 entries per layer is just a warning line. At the hard ceiling a save is never refused: the least recently read entry in the same layer moves to archive (pinned rules are never evicted) and the result names it (body and full record kept, restorable by hand); only an entry that alone exceeds the budget fails. Saying 「别记」 also archives. Files are never deleted.
- One directory per project, so projects never see each other's notes.

## 项目自进化〔实验〕 / Project self-evolution (experimental)

默认关闭，只对当前项目生效。开启后，它从你的纠正和认可里整理出少量项目规范：纠正更新做法，认可作品只给已有规范留一条带维度的样例；执行漏掉只补检查点，不改写成禁令。下次匹配任务按需读取，不逐轮注入。会增加一次有上限的后台整理调用，以及命中的记忆读取消耗。

Off by default, per project only. When enabled it distills a few project rules from your corrections and approvals: corrections revise the approach, approvals attach one bounded sample to an existing rule, and an execution miss adds a checkpoint instead of a ban. Matching tasks read them on demand, never per turn. It adds one bounded background organize call and the memory reads that actually hit.

- 一次整理最多 2 处改动、768 输出 token、15 秒；输入不超过 8 KiB，同一作品最多 2 次，同一项目 24 小时内最多 6 次。
- 成果停在 `pending` / `trial` / `active` / `paused`；明确说「以后都这样」或两个独立作品支持才 `active`，试用与暂停 30 天后清理。试用会参与条件匹配任务的读取，不是预览稿；到期自动暂停。
- 规则 32 条、待定 12 条、每规则样例 4 个/检查点 3 个/来源 3 条、旧版本 2 个，都有硬上限；到顶先暂停新学习，不静默丢已生效规则。
- 面板显示整理次数和已知用量；usage 没返回就写未知，不补零。
- 关闭后停止学习、读取和晚到写入；成果保留可查看。记忆总开关关闭时自进化一定也是关闭，不能单独打开。
- 同一项目换栏目、新一期、临时例外不会互相继承；仓库子目录、符号链接、worktree 视为同一项目，不同克隆分开。

- At most 2 changes, 768 output tokens and 15 s per organize call; input ≤ 8 KiB, ≤ 2 calls per episode and ≤ 6 per project in 24 h.
- Results stay `pending` / `trial` / `active` / `paused`; they become `active` only on an explicit long-term ask or two independent episodes; trial and paused entries expire after 30 days. A trial is read by matching tasks — it is not a preview — and pauses when it expires.
- Hard caps: 32 rules, 12 pending, 4 samples / 3 checkpoints / 3 sources per rule, 2 old versions. At the ceiling new learning pauses; active explicit rules are never silently dropped.
- The panel reports organize calls and known usage; missing usage is shown as unknown, never zero.
- Turning it off stops learning, reads and late writes; results stay viewable. While project memory is off, self-evolution is necessarily off and cannot be switched on by itself.
- Switching columns, a new episode and one-off exceptions do not leak into each other; a repository subdirectory, symlink or worktree is the same project, separate clones are not.

## 发布候选 / Release candidate

- 全链路审计结论与轻量化数字：[`docs/RC-0.18.46.md`](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/docs/RC-0.18.46.md)
- 基准复现：`npm run bench`、`npm run bench:evolution`，基线见 [`docs/BENCH.md`](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/docs/BENCH.md)

## 安装 / Install

Plugin Manager 里搜 `dsh-lite-memory` 直接装；或 `npm pack` 后用 Plugin Manager 安装生成的 `.tgz`。

Install from the DSH Plugin Manager (search `dsh-lite-memory`), or `npm pack` and install the resulting `.tgz` through it.

## 工具 / Tools

`memory_save` · `memory_suggest` · `memory_search` · `memory_read` · `memory_forget`

完整触发规则见 [TRIGGERS.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/TRIGGERS.md)，内部判定契约（准入顺序、状态码、写入/更新/失败语义）见 [docs/CONVENTIONS.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/docs/CONVENTIONS.md)；性能与 UI 门禁的实测数字见 [docs/BENCH.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/docs/BENCH.md)。 / Full trigger rules: [TRIGGERS.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/TRIGGERS.md); internal decision contract: [docs/CONVENTIONS.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/docs/CONVENTIONS.md); measured performance and UI-gate evidence: [docs/BENCH.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-lite-memory/blob/HEAD/docs/BENCH.md).

# dsh-inner-browser-use

一个由 agent 自己养的 Chrome，实时投到 DeepSeek Harness 的右栏里。

agent 打开网页、读页面、点、输入、滚动。这个浏览器是独立的 Chrome 进程，用自己的磁盘
profile，不是产品自带的那个浏览页签：右栏放的是它的画面，而画面上的鼠标仍然是你自己的。

## 工具

| 工具 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_open` | 启动浏览器（已在跑就复用）并打开一个地址。传 `headless: false` 会改为在桌面上开真实窗口。 |
| `browser_view` | 返回地址、标题、编号成 `1 … 120` 的控件，以及可见文字。 |
| `browser_read` | 按人读文章的方式给 Markdown（标题、段落、列表、链接）。带 `query` 只回能回答的那几句（段落排序后再按句子打分，标题、位置、链接密度做先验，重复句去掉，按字符预算装箱）；问不到时只回最近的三段并明说没答上，不再把整页端回来；当前页答不上来还会顺手读这个会话自己开着的其它页签，答案在哪页就从哪页回并标出页签标题（bench 里少 90% 字符），`across: false` 只读当前页。页面和上次读的没变就只回一行，不重发正文（`force: true` 强制重发）。 |
| `browser_extract` | 按 CSS 选择器把列表项读成一行一条、带链接，比整页读省得多。 |
| `browser_view` 的 `map` | 大页面先看地标：各类控件各多少个、去重后的控件和编号、正文多少字，但不带回正文。 |
| `browser_click` | 点编号控件，或点 `x`/`y` 坐标。`double: true` 双击。控件被横幅或弹层挡着时，先关掉它再点。 |
| `browser_type` | 往焦点输入框输入文字，也可以先点一个编号控件。中文整段送进去。`submit: true` 回车提交。 |
| `browser_key` | 按一个键：Enter、Tab、Escape、Backspace、Delete、上下左右、Home、End、PageUp、PageDown。 |
| `browser_scroll` | 在页面中心滚轮，也可以指定 `x`/`y`。`dy: 600` 约一屏。 |
| `browser_shot` | 存一张 PNG 到 `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/screenshots`，返回路径；`region: [x, y, w, h]` 只截一块（游戏、图表、看局部）。 |
| `browser_look` | 看自己画自己的页面（游戏、canvas、Flash）：把画面压成字母网格，一块屏幕一个字母、同色同字母，12×8 约 200 字符，不花图片 token；再看一次只报变了的格子。要颜色、布局或给人看图仍用 `browser_shot`。 |
| `browser_media` | 列出页面已经请求过的视频和声音（带大小），页面自己播放器里那个排第一、标 `main`；`save: <行号>`、`save: main` 或地址片段存下来。广告和统计默认不出现（`all: true` 才看），`watch: false` 关掉这个页面的记录。流会顺着播放列表把片段取回拼好，不用装任何东西。 |
| `browser_login` | 按名字留住登录：`save` 存下当前窗口的 cookie 和各站的 localStorage，`list` 看有哪些，`use` 切回那个账号并重开页面，`import` 把本机 Chrome/Brave/Edge 里已经登着的站直接留成一个名字，`drop` 忘掉。名字跟着浏览器走、不跟着一个会话走，重启也在；同一站点两个账号就存两个名字。磁盘上那一份是加密的，钥匙在系统钥匙串里。 |
| `browser_state` | 报浏览器在不在跑、用的哪个 profile、地址、标题、有几个右栏在看它，以及它此刻占多少内存、没人用的话还有多久关闭。 |

同一个站读两次就会被按 origin 记住（`~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/sites.json`，可用 `DSH_INNER_BROWSER_STATE_DIR` 改位置）。第二次之后：正文或控件多的站，`browser_view` 默认先给 `map:` 地标；文章长的站，`browser_read` 默认截到 3500 字符并说明截在哪。两者都带一句实测数字，也都会被显式 `mode`、`query`、`max_chars` 覆盖——学到的是默认值，不是对直接提问的答案。`scripts/check-sites.mjs` 是现场证据：300 个按钮的页看三次、12000 字的文档读三次，报出截断位置。

点、输入、按键之后的那一行会多一句结果：`· navigated to …`（换页了）、`· content changed`（页内有变化）、`· no visible change`（点了没动）、Flash 页则是 `· screen updated` / `· no frame change`；`read: true` 时不再多说。

`browser_view` 一次给一页文本：

```
https://example.com
Example Domain

1 [a] More information
7 [input] Search
```

编号到下一次读之前都有效。任何改动页面的操作都会顺带返回一次新的读取。

## 右栏

那一栏显示的是浏览器的画面，按会话自己的流发 JPEG：1440×900，质量 72，每帧都发；静止
页面上约 82 KB 一帧、每秒 25 帧。

画面上有两个指针：

- **黑色箭头是 agent。** 它标在 agent 上一次点击的落点上，新的点击一发出箭头就动，不等
  页面重绘。
- **鼠标是你自己的。** 悬停、点击、滚轮、按键都当作真实输入交给浏览器，所以对拦截脚本点击
  的站也照常管用。移动鼠标不会带动黑色箭头。

画面上方那行地址就是地址栏：输入域名回车，页面换成它；旁边是后退、前进、刷新。你在编辑时
它不会跟着页面跳。

输入分两路进来：输入法合成的文字（中文、emoji 等）整段插入，按键则按原样送过去，所以
Backspace 在页面上删掉的是一个字。

右栏只在向它要过页面的那个会话里打开。别的会话调用工具时用的是同一个浏览器，但不会抢走
别人正在看的这一栏。

## 登录态

profile 是独立目录：`~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/chrome/default`。它在产品自己的浏览数据之外
——那份数据是每个进程临时建的，进程一退就没了，所以在这里登过的账号第二天还在。

- **插件重载。** 重载会接上仍在运行的那个 Chrome，页面也还在原处。
- **Harness 重启。** 重新打开同一个目录，cookie、`localStorage` 和 Chrome 存下的密码都留着。
- **退出。** 关浏览器是请它自己关（`Browser.close`），Chrome 在这一步才把 cookie 落盘。

## 借用本机 Chrome 的登录

起的是这台机器上同一个 Google Chrome，只是 `--user-data-dir` 指到上面那个目录，所以 cookie
格式和加密方式和你日常用的 Chrome 完全一致——登录能直接搬过来：打开要进的那个站，一次
`browser_login {action:"import", name:"work"}`，插件去读 Chrome 的 cookie 库（读副本，不动
原文件，也不要求你关掉 Chrome），用钥匙串里的 Chrome Safe Storage 解开该站的 cookie，封进
自己的保险库；之后 `use` 把它注回去并重开页面，跨会话都在。

不共享 profile 目录：Chrome 对 profile 是单例锁，你开着它就打不开；打开还会因为扩展和版本
差异改动你的数据。所以只搬该站的 cookie（和 localStorage，`save` 时一并存），不复制整个
profile，也不上传。

macOS 会挡这一步：Chrome 的 profile 在系统保护范围内，直接读是 `Operation not permitted`。
需要给 DSH 开 **系统设置 → 隐私与安全性 → 完全磁盘访问权限**。没开时工具会原样说出来。

## 常驻成本

同机、同量法（同一台本地 fixture、同一档无头 Chrome，一次只跑一家），对照五家：
Playwright MCP、Chrome DevTools MCP、Stagehand、browser-use——都只量不用模型的那一层，
拿自己的确定性实现去和别人的推理延迟比没有意义。空闲 RSS **459–552 MB**（对方
1265–1672）、空闲 CPU **0.03–0.47%**（36–51%）；休息后唤醒 **0.39–0.59 s** 回到原页，
对方要整棵重启 4.6–5.1 s；同一个页面本插件读 **2302 字符**，对方 5662–21396。开到 6 个页签时
**864–922 MB**、每页约 +2 MB、始终 4 个渲染进程、空闲 0.9%（稳态 0.24%）一个核。热浏览器里
再开一页，工具层中位 **42–54 ms**，其中 `openTab` 内部的页签启动只要 **20 ms**（browser-use
裸 `new_page` 是 24–33 ms）。一张截图 **51 ms**，与五家的 48–71 ms 一样（成本在 Chrome 自己的
抓帧与编码），但回来的是一条路径加 223 字符，不是对方塞进回答的 100–383 KB base64。
没赢的地方也写在文档里：冷启动 **840 ms**（701–936）对 Stagehand 760、browser-use 713，
因为那两家把 Chrome 起在自己进程里。`npm run bench` 与 `npm run tabs` 可复现，
五家对照明细在 `docs/BENCH.md`。

## 没人看的时候

每两秒用一次的人，两分钟后就休息；每九十秒用一次的人能等九分钟——窗口取自这个人最近 64 次
调用间隔的 95 分位，休息乘 6、可逆停驻乘 2，是学出来的不是配出来的。右栏关掉后一分钟就真的
释放（内存归零，cookies 先存好）；右栏还开着只是没人动，就走停驻——DOM、滚动位置、登录态都
留着，截图流停掉。唤醒 0.3–1.1 秒，回到同一个地址。无头验证跑 `npm run rest`，内存阶梯与
竞品对照在 `docs/RESOURCES.md`。

profile 之外只写一样东西：`~/.dsh-inner-browser-use/screenshots/` 里的截图。

## 实测

| | |
| --- | --- |
| 打开页面到第一帧 | 约 850 ms，含网络加载 |
| 单帧 | 1440×900 JPEG，约 82 KB |
| 画面 | 约 25 帧每秒 |
| 指针移动到箭头跟上 | 0.8–7 ms |
| 右栏里手动点击到画面更新 | 中位 13 ms，最坏 17 ms（点击派发 2 ms、悬停 8 ms） |

## 安装

```bash
git clone https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-inner-browser-use
dsh plugin install /path/to/dsh-inner-browser-use
```

在应用里走 **插件 → 从文件夹安装**，选这个仓库目录。要装打包好的 tgz，就在该目录里打一个再装：

```bash
npm pack                                  # 得到 dsh-inner-browser-use-0.12.1.tgz
dsh plugin install ./dsh-inner-browser-use-0.12.1.tgz
```

装好后在 **插件** 里显示为 *后台浏览器*。机器上要有 Google Chrome 或 Chromium，细节见
[docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-inner-browser-use/blob/HEAD/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md)。

## 使用

1. 打开你想让 agent 代跑的会话。
2. 直接说要页面上的什么事：*「打开 example.com，告诉我标题」*。

第一次调用会启动浏览器，并把镜像放进这个会话的右栏。没有调用就不会有东西自己打开：没要过
页面的会话，右栏保持原样。

## Flash 页面

`browser_open` 带 `flash: true` 时，这个地址改用插件自带的 Flash 运行时（Electron 87 + Pepper Flash）在**离屏窗口**里播放：窗口一次都不显示，Dock 与菜单栏都不出现，画面只在发起会话的右栏里。切换回来再调一次 `flash: false`，选择会记住。运行时首次使用时下载到 `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/flash/`，不需要单独安装播放器。

`npm run flash-hidden` 会真起一次运行时并断言「窗口未显示 / 帧持续产出 / 两帧不同」；`npm run flash-mirror` 量镜像帧率与按下/抬起/按键耗时；`npm run flash-tools` 量工具层成本（奥拉星登录页实测：点击 28 ms、输入 14 ms、`browser_view` 31 ms；同一页后续回话只说标题，点击 22 字符、输入 13 字符）；`npm run flash-local` 用仓库自带的 SWF 在本机起页，不依赖网络，量首帧与输入直达。

## 框架、下载、网络

- **iframe 能读，跨站也能。** 不管是和页面共用进程，还是 Chrome 单独给一个进程，里面的控件都和页面自己的控件一样有编号；点击按框架在页面上的实际位置落点。
- **下载会落到磁盘。** 点一下就下载的文件写在这个浏览器自己的 profile 目录里，`browser_downloads` 报出文件名、大小和到达时间。
- **PDF 有去处。** Chrome 无头进程画不出 PDF，右栏只会是白图；读到 PDF 时把文件取回归档到该浏览器 profile 的 `downloads/`，结果里直接给绝对路径，交给 `envoy_read` 或本地阅读器。
- **能看到网络。** `browser_network` 倒序列出页面请求了什么，自己用接口填内容、屏幕上又看不出原因的页面，不用截图去猜。
- **遮罩不吞动作。** 盖在按钮上的 cookie 横幅会按人的做法先关掉再点下去，同一次调用里完成；`browser_do` 的每一步都一样。写着删除、支付、退出的遮罩只报告，不代按。

## 不做什么

- **不动你自己的 Chrome。** 浏览器跑在单独的 profile 上，和你正在用的窗口没有关系。
- **视口固定。** 1440×900、桌面布局，不缩放，也不模拟手机。
- **一次一页。** 点开新页签的链接会被跟过去：镜像落到新页面，弹窗随即关掉，不会留下第二个页面要选。

[![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)



[安装](#安装) · [效果预览](#效果预览) · [配置](#在-dsh-设置里改配置) · [兼容性](#兼容性) · [已知限制](#已知限制) · [更新日志](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)

DSH Web / Desktop 的通知插件，让你敢不开完整访问，也不必一直守着页面。

- **需要你操作时**：审批、方案确认、提问，用通知、提示音和标题标记提醒。
- **后台回复完成时**：及时回来查看结果，点击通知可回到对应对话；提醒时机可选「仅后台 / 仅当前对话静默 / 总是提醒」。
- **人走开但窗口没走**：窗口留在最前台、人却离开座位，超过 3 分钟没有输入也算离开，该提醒的照常提醒；收到的那条通知不会在你回来之前自己消失，一回到页面（点任务栏、Alt+Tab、点通知都算）就收起。
- **离开电脑时**：可选转发到 Discord、Bark、Gotify、飞书群机器人、Server酱、WxPusher 或自己的 Webhook。
- **连页面都关掉时**：可选让宿主进程兜底——页面不在时宿主继续把「需要你操作」「回复完成」推到你的网关；也可以只开同源中继，让页面够到要认证的网关。两项默认关，配置写在 profile 的 patch 层（见[高级设置](#高级设置)里的「页面关闭后：宿主侧兜底与同源中继」）。

> 页面或桌面应用需保持运行（后台 / 最小化可以）；系统通知需要通知权限。审批按钮依赖 Service Worker，只有 Web 端有，桌面端的通知不带按钮，点通知回到对话里裁决。开启宿主侧兜底后，页面关闭仍能收到外部推送——本地通知与审批按钮仍要页面在。
