## 安装

**方式一：GitHub 直装（推荐）**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:drscrewdriver/dsh-browser-cdp
# 也可锁定到某个 commit / tag：
dsh plugin --profile web add github:drscrewdriver/dsh-browser-cdp#v0.9.0
```

> `github:` 安装由 pnpm 经 `codeload.github.com` 拉取仓库 tarball，**无需向 npm registry 发包**；直接使用仓库中**预构建入库的 `lib/`**（`files` 仅含 `lib/`、`bin/`、`runtime/`、`cordis.patch.yml`、`dsh-plugin.json`），因此**不触发任何构建脚本**，也不需要 devDependencies。host 入口 `lib/index.js`、客户端 `lib/client.js`、worker `bin/cdp-cast-worker.mjs` 均随仓库分发。

**方式二：本地 tarball / git URL**

```sh
dshx install dsh-browser-cdp <dsh-browser-cdp.tgz>      # tarball 或 git URL 均可
dshx list                                                # 应显示：[on] dsh-browser-cdp
```

> **包名迁移说明**：本插件包名是 **`dsh-browser-cdp`**（曾用名 `dsh-ego-browser`、别名 `@dsh-external/ego-browser`）。DSH Desktop 2.0.5 起增加了「profile 依赖名 == 包实际 name」的一致性校验，若 profile 仍用旧名引用，启动会挂进恢复模式。升级后请把 profile 的 `package.json` 依赖键 **和** `dsh.profile.bundles` 条目**两处**都改为 `dsh-browser-cdp`：

   ```diff
   - "dsh-ego-browser": "<旧 github 来源>",
   + "dsh-browser-cdp": "github:drscrewdriver/dsh-browser-cdp",
   ```

   ```diff
   - "dsh-ego-browser",
   + "dsh-browser-cdp",
   ```

观察窗设置中可选 `captureBackend=auto|cdp|ffmpeg`（默认 `auto`，当前解析为 CDP）、画质档位、CDP FPS/JPEG 质量/最大宽度，以及 FFmpeg FPS/最大宽度/码率/编码器/自定义路径。插件先检测自定义路径、系统 PATH 和托管缓存；GitHub 下载可用 `githubMirror` 替换 `https://github.com`，例如 `https://gh-proxy.com/github.com`。FFmpeg 码率范围为 500-20000 kbps，低/平衡/高档默认 2000/4000/8000 kbps。

无需宿主侧任何配置：`resolveEgoEnv` 自动探测 root / 无显示器并兜底。观察窗 host 路由（`/api/bcdp/spaces` 等）仅在有 HTTP server 时注册，headless 是安全 no-op。

## 连接方式：CDP 端点 / 本机 ego CLI / 本机 Tabbit CLI / Lightpanda

**连接目标直接在设置里增删改**（0.18.1 起，与 0.17.x 线同源）：设置卡有两处入口——「起子插件设置」family 区的本插件 tab（装了 `dsh-thinking-levels` 时），以及**插件详情页**的设置卡（`plugins.bundle.config`，不装 thinking-levels 时的独立入口）；两处渲染同一份组件。每行支持：启用开关、激活、标签/端点/CLI 路径就位编辑、逐行**探测**、上移/下移、删除（删激活行会同时清空激活，**绝不顺延**）；底部内联表单直接添加 CDP 端点、本机 ego CLI、Lightpanda 或本机 Tabbit CLI（第二条本机 CLI / Tabbit 行会被拒绝）。写回落在活动 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`，跨重启保留。0.18.1 之前，连接序列只能在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` `links` 中手工维护。

设置面板里的连接列表是**有序**的——**顺序即优先级**，被激活的那一项驱动每一次 `bcdp_*` 调用。列表元素有四种类型：

| 类型 | 它做什么 | 约束 |
|---|---|---|
| **CDP 端点** | 把一个已开调试端口的浏览器地址交给内置运行时（注入 `EGO_LINUX_CDP_URL`），运行时**附着**上去 | 可多条 |
| **本机 ego CLI** | 由本机 ego CLI **自己**驱动它本机的 ego 浏览器——**不注入任何端点** | **仅限本机，全局至多一条** |
| **本机 Tabbit CLI** | 由本机 `tabbit-cli` 驱动它本机的 Tabbit 浏览器（`tabbit-cli nodejs` 执行 Playwright 片段）——**不走插件的裸 CDP 通道** | **仅限本机，全局至多一条** |
| **Lightpanda** | 插件托管启动的无头文本渲染引擎（详见下节），对插件而言是一个普通 CDP 端点 | 全局至多一条 |

**为什么需要第二种**：注入用的 `EGO_LINUX_CDP_URL` 是**内置运行时（Linux 线）**的私有契约，macOS 上用 `ego lite` app 附带的那个原生 `ego-browser` **根本不读它**。所以在只有"CDP 端点"这一种类型时，macOS 用户无法用上自己那个已登录的 ego——只能连远端端口，或让内置运行时另起一个 stock Chromium。本机 CLI 类型补的就是这条路。Tabbit 行则是同类需求的另一条：**只有 `tabbit-cli` 能驱 Tabbit 自己的任务生命周期**（CLI 不对外开调试端口），所以插件不做裸 CDP 而是拼 Playwright 片段下发（详见下节「Tabbit 后端」）。

解析顺序（`cliPath` 留空时）：显式路径 → PATH 上的 `ego-browser` → macOS app 包内 helper（`/Applications/ego lite.app/…/Helpers/ego-browser`）→ 插件内置运行时。Tabbit 行的解析顺序（`cliPath` 留空时）：显式路径 → `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Tabbit\LocalAgent\bin\tabbit-cli(.exe)`（Windows）→ `~/.local/bin` / `/usr/local/bin`（macOS/Linux）→ PATH 探测。

三个默认值值得知道：

- **`useSdkPath` 默认关闭**：关闭时用 CLI 自带的 harness（配套的那套）；打开后，**探测与每一次工具执行**都会注入 `--sdk-path <插件内置 harness>`。这一点很关键：只在探测时带、执行时不带，脚本首行就会崩 `ReferenceError: taskSpaces is not defined`（1.2.4 修复的 P0）。若 CLI 不认这个旗标，探测会记一条提示并**自动重试一次不带它**；此时只有 CLI 自带的 harness 确实暴露 `taskSpaces` / `browser` 门面才算就绪，否则显式判失败并给出缺失的门面名——不再假阳性。
- **就绪探测是 `nodejs` 通道上的 facade 探针**（与干活同一条通道）：只检查注入后的 `taskSpaces` / `browser` / `page` 全局，不启动也不等待浏览器，实测约 300 ms；`bcdp_status` 走同一判据。
- **Tabbit 的 `--timeout-ms` 被夹紧到 60000–180000**：超出范围 CLI 直接整请求拒绝（snippet 根本不执行），所以下发前在一处夹紧到最近合法值；单帧/截图的短截止不由它表达，而是写在 snippet 内的 `Promise.race`（默认 8s 截止，超时返回 `skipped: capture-timeout`）。

### 双 API 面共存风险

本插件通过注入 SDK 使用 `taskSpaces.*`（插件侧 API），而 `ego-browser skill` 脚本使用原生 `taskSpace()`（app 侧 API）。二者驱动的是**同一个** ego，task space 也是共享的：同时用插件工具和该 skill 脚本操作同一空间，可能互相抢控制权。**建议二选一，以插件为准**；确需跑该 skill 脚本时，先停用本插件的 ego-cli link。

与其它开关的关系：

- `cdpMode`：`auto` 按激活项（四种类型都行）；`remote` **只接受 CDP 端点**，激活项是本机 CLI / Tabbit 时会显式报 `mode-kind-mismatch`；`local` 走受管本地启动器。
- `remoteEnabled`（远端总开关）**只管远端 CDP**，不影响本机 CLI / Tabbit 连接。
- `allowLocalFallback` / `localHeadless` / `localUserDataDir` 只作用于 CDP 端点的回落与受管启动。
- `allowProbeColdStart`（**默认关**）：就绪探测**绝不拉起 ego 浏览器**——`--status` 证明浏览器已在跑才做 heredoc 验证，否则跳过，浏览器推迟到首个真实 `bcdp_*` 调用才启动（插件挂载/改设置不再弹浏览器窗口）。打开 = 挂载探测预先验证 SDK harness（可能当场弹出浏览器窗口）。

`bcdp_doctor` 会报告当前序列类型计数、CLI 实际解析到的路径与形态，以及（若同机装了旧版 `dsh-ego-browser`）一条共存提示。

> 现行口径：doctor 的 `links:` 计数行只列 cdp / ego-cli / lightpanda 三种，**tabbit 行不计入该行**；Tabbit 作激活后端时以 `bcdp_status` / `bcdp_help` 报出的 `backend: tabbit-cli` 为准。

## Tabbit 后端（本机 Tabbit 浏览器，可选通道）

[Tabbit 浏览器](https://github.com/Tabbit-Browser)本身是 Chromium，但本插件不直接拿它的调试端口：激活 `tabbit-cli` 连接行后，每次 `bcdp_*` 调用被翻译成一段 Playwright 片段，经 `tabbit-cli nodejs` 在浏览器内嵌运行时里执行（适配层 `src/cdp/tabbit-cli-link.ts`）。也就是说 Tabbit 是**第四条连接通道**，与 CDP 端点 / 本机 ego CLI / Lightpanda 并列，按列表优先级争用。

- **添加入口**：设置面板底部表单选「本机 Tabbit CLI」（默认标签 `Tabbit 浏览器`）；第二会被拒绝。`cliPath` 留空走上方的自动解析链。
- **支持的工具**（1.7.10 现行口径）：`bcdp_space`、`bcdp_navigate`、`bcdp_snapshot`、`bcdp_click`、`bcdp_fill`、`bcdp_screenshot`、`bcdp_tab op=list`，以及入口类 `bcdp_status` / `bcdp_help` / `bcdp_doctor`。**未覆盖的工具明确报错而不静默回落 Chrome**——激活 Tabbit 时插件会硬拒内置运行时启动（避免“以为在 Tabbit 里做、实际驱动了另一个浏览器”）。
- **能力降级由连接模式决定**（`src/cdp/capabilities.ts` 的 `tabbit` 投影）：`Browser.*` / `Target.*` 域不可达→无标签枚举与窗口关闭；Overlay 点选不可用→观察窗不能“点选元素引用进输入框”；下载事件不可用→`bcdp_download` 不可用；`Runtime.addBinding` 不可靠→`bindingCalled` 关闭。画面与截图走 page 作域的 `newCDPSession` + `Page.captureScreenshot`，JPEG 原生可用。
- **观察窗画面**：与内置运行时非 CDP 连接模式同一机制——后台轮询而非 screencast 直推，间隔 3s；重页面上单帧捕获可能贴近 8s 截止线（实测），所以高负载页面的实际刷新率会低于 3s，卡住的帧以 `skipped` 返回而不是挂死面板。
- **与 dsh-tabbit 插件的关系**：两者都能驱 Tabbit，但工具面与任务生命周期各自管理。同机共装时建议**二选一**，避免两个 harness 抢同一个 Tabbit 任务槽。

## Lightpanda 后端（可选引擎，beta）

[Lightpanda](https://lightpanda.io) 是面向 AI 的无头文本渲染浏览器（AGPL-3.0，本插件仅作 CDP 客户端使用）。它对插件来说就是一个**普通 CDP 端点**：设置面板添加并激活后，probe 会从 `/json/version` 的 `Browser: Lightpanda/…` **自动识别引擎**，badge 与 `bcdp_doctor` 显示 engine，能力降级自动生效（无需任何配置）。

### 分系统安装

| 系统 | 方式 |
|---|---|
| **Linux**（建议本机直装测试） | `curl -fsSL https://pkg.lightpanda.io/install.sh \| bash`（装入 `~/.local/bin`，确保 PATH 含它）→ `lightpanda serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9222` |
| **macOS**（建议本机直装测试） | 同上一键脚本（aarch64）→ 同 serve 命令 |
| **Windows**（内置方案 = WSL2，无原生版） | 管理员 PowerShell `wsl --install` → 重启 → `wsl --install -d Ubuntu` → WSL 内同 Linux 一键脚本 → WSL 内 `lightpanda serve …`；WSL2 自动把端口映射到 Windows localhost（**二进制只存在于 WSL 内，宿主侧没有文件，属预期**） |
| **Docker（备选）** | `docker run -d --name lightpanda -p 127.0.0.1:9222:9222 lightpanda/browser:nightly` |

装好后在本插件设置面板添加 CDP 端点 `http://127.0.0.1:9222` 并激活即可。可选：`export LIGHTPANDA_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true` 关遥测。

### 能力降级矩阵（识别后自动生效）

| 能力 | Lightpanda 上的行为 |
|---|---|
| 导航 / JS / 点击 / 填表 / 键鼠 / 快照（AX 树）/ HTTP / 登录导入 / 等待族 | **无损可用** |
| `bcdp_screenshot` | PNG **文本级渲染**（无像素引擎，视觉保真低于 Chrome；runtime 本就发 png，零改动兼容） |
| jev 视觉链（`bcdp_jev_frame` 等） | 投影自动改发 PNG；输出带 `engine` / `rendering: text` 元数据 |
| 观察窗实时画面 | **关闭**——无 screencast 且无窗口，worker 不启动采集循环，面板显示降级提示 |
| 面板点选（inspect 路径） | **关闭**——无 Overlay 域 / bindingCalled 事件，返回 `engine-unsupported`（i18n）；坐标回退路径保留 |
| `bcdp_download` | **关闭**——无 Page 下载事件，调用即返回结构化错误（不会挂起超时） |
| `bcdp_auth_flush` | 返回 `degraded: true`——引擎无 `Storage.flushCookies`，cookie 仅随引擎进程存活 |

识别失败的端点（`engine: unknown`）保持**全能力**——误判只应"少给"，不应"错给"。

### 1.5.0 迁移表（旧名 → 新调用）

wait / space / escape 三族已按 `op` 合并，旧工具名**移除**（不保留别名——别名同样吃 schema 预算，等于没省）。其余工具名不变。

| `bcdp_wait_for_url` `{pattern, timeout}` | `bcdp_wait` `{op:"url", pattern, timeout}` |

> `op` 合并后各 op 的必需参数写在工具描述里；缺参会返回带 op 名的 `reason`（如 `bcdp_wait: selector is required for op=selector`），不会静默降级。

## 工具注入分级（懒注册 / 分级 / 锁定）

34 个工具全量注册时，**每个会话每一轮**都要为它们的 schema 付费（挂载级实测 `description` + `parameters` 序列化 = **24,631 字符** ≈ 7.1K token，1.7.0；1.5.0 曾测为 22,224，增量主要来自分级文档与工具描述互斥引导）。而不碰浏览器的会话一个也用不上。插件因此把「谁能出现在模型面前」收成一处策略（`src/toolTiers.ts`），分**八批**注入。

> **8 批 ≠ 8 个开关**。批次是*注入时机*，开关是*用户面*（§9.3「开关与批次解耦」）。当前 4 个开关管 8 批：`toolBrowse` 管 act+observe+wait 三批并按波次放行，`toolExtended` 管 power+session，`toolEscape`、`toolJudge` 各管一批。所以「`toolBrowse` = 19 个」指的是**并集上限**，实际第一波只放 13 个。

| 批次 | 成员 | schema | 何时出现 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **core** 常驻（1） | `bcdp_status` | 401 | 永远在场，不可封印——它是 lazy 唯一的解锁入口 |
| **act** 动手（13） | space / navigate / click / fill / key / hover / scroll / select / check / drag / tab / help / doctor | 8,762 | `lazy` 下首次活动放第一波 |
| **observe** 观察（5） | screenshot / page_info / read_element / js / snapshot | 3,109 | 第二次活动 |
| **wait** 等待（1） | `bcdp_wait`（duration / selector / url / response / load / function / request / event） | 1,976 | 第三次活动 |
| **power** 重量级（5） | raw CDP / http / upload / download / dialog | 3,692 | 首次活动（同 `toolExtended`） |
| **session** 登录态（3） | captcha / auth_flush / login_import | 1,864 | 首次活动（同 `toolExtended`） |
| **escape** 逃生舱（1） | `bcdp_script`（`verbatim:true` = 原 cli 的裸 heredoc） | 1,484 | 首次活动（1.7.0 起不再吃活动闸豁免，见下） |
| **judge** 评审链（5） | `bcdp_jev_*` | 3,343 | 除解锁外，**还要求配了 JEV 或 Laya Key** |
| **合计** | 34 | **24,631** | — |

> 表内 schema 与合计均为 1.7.0 **挂载级实测**（`tests/tier-mount.test.ts` 的度量用例打印），八批求和 = 24,631 与全量档逐字对齐。

设置项在插件设置页**最上方**的「工具封印」分块（全部 volatile，翻完当场生效，不重启插件）——一个开关管一组批次，形状照 dsh-prime-memory 的「工具封印」：

- **`toolInjection`** `lazy`（**默认**：只常驻 `bcdp_status`——它是唯一的解锁入口，其余首次 `bcdp_*` 调用后按开关注入）/ `always`（挂载即全量，历史行为）。
- **`toolBrowse`**（act + observe + wait = 19）/ **`toolExtended`**（power + session = 8）/ **`toolEscape`**（script = 1）/ **`toolJudge`**（5）：开 = 开放注册，关 = 该批从模型工具列表移除。四组各自独立，封一组不波及别组；`core` 级不给开关（封了就没了活动入口）。

**1.7.0 起 `escape` 不再吃活动闸的例外**：`bcdp_script` 仍是唯一能在一次调用里干完任意多步任务的入口（`page` / `browser` / `taskSpaces` / `fetch` / `cdp` 全预置），但它不再常驻——先调一次常驻的 `bcdp_status` 即可拿到它。豁免的代价是它单独占 ≈1,700 字符/轮（比收窄后的整个常驻面还大四轮），而 lazy 会话里模型本来就要先调 `status`。如果你需要「冷启动直接写脚本」的旧行为，设 `toolInjection = always`（或留在 1.6.x）。

行为要点：

- **封印 = 反注册**（工具从模型的工具列表里消失），不是执行期拒绝。解锁信号挂在 `bcdp_*` 调用的公共出口上，工具体不知道分级存在；`bcdp_status` / `bcdp_help` / `bcdp_doctor` 自身也算活动信号（读了指南就得有工具可用）——但后两者已属 act 批，冷启动下只能靠 `bcdp_status` 触发。
- **闲置自动收回**：`lazy` + `idleTimeoutMin > 0` 时，空闲回收把后台浏览器停掉的同一刻收回扩展面；下次活动重新铺开。`always` 模式不受影响。
- `legacyEgoToolNames` 的 `ego_*` 别名跟随其 `bcdp_*` 本体的级别。
- 当前注入面写在 `bcdp_doctor` 报告首行（例：`tool injection: mode=lazy browse=open extended=open escape=open judge=open judgeKey=none active=yes → live 28 / sealed 6`，即一次 `bcdp_status` + 一次 `doctor` 之后的面），不用猜。注意 `doctor` 本身已属 act 批，要先调 `bcdp_status` 才能拿到它；冷启动时模型面上只有 `bcdp_status`（live 1 / sealed 33）。
- 默认档下不碰浏览器的会话只有 **1** 个工具在场（`bcdp_status` = 401 字符 ≈115 tok，较 1.5.0 的 4,978 字符 **−91.9%**）；它是解锁入口，调用即按批次铺开其余工具。要回到历史行为把 `toolInjection` 改成 `always`（34 件全在场需再配一个评审 Key）。
- **各档实测注入面**（挂载级口径，1.7.0；序列化工具的 `name + description + parameters` 求和，token 按 3.48 字符/token 折算）：默认 **1 个 / 401 字符 ≈115 tok** → 首次活动（act 批 + power + session + escape）23 个 / 16,203 ≈4,660 tok → 第 2 波（+observe）与第 3 波（+wait）后 29 个 / 21,288 ≈6,120 tok → 全量（always + 评审 Key）34 个 / 24,631 ≈7,080 tok。这些数字由 `tests/tier-mount.test.ts` 的度量用例当场打印，不靠估算。
- 五个字段都带 schema `.default()`：volatile 字段的表单描述符直接拿 schema 默认值，不写默认会出现「面板显示 A、运行时用 B」。

> 取舍提醒：窄工具（一个动作一个工具）是模型写对参数、少重试的护栏。1.5.0 只合并了 **wait / space / escape** 三族同源冗余（41 → 34，省 1,869 字符 schema）：五个 wait 共用同一 preamble 与 timeout 语义、三个 space 本就是同一个 op 工具的碎片、cli/script 是同一 heredoc 运行时。代价是这三族的旧工具名不再存在（见上方迁移表）；交互原子（click/fill/key…）**不合并**，因为它们是模型写对参数的护栏。

## 任务空间命名与并发隔离（1.6.0）

> **默认就是会话隔离**：不传 `space` 的调用落在**本会话自己的**任务空间 `dsh-agent-<会话id前8位>`，两个会话永远不会共用或抢占同一个浏览上下文。**只有显式写 `space: 'default'`（或 `bcdp_space op=open name='default'`）才会用那个跨会话共享的具名槽。**

| 你怎么写 | 落到哪个空间 |
|---|---|
| 省略 `space`（默认，`defaultSpace` 未设 = `:auto`） | `dsh-agent-<会话id前8位>`，每会话独立 |
| `space: 'default'` / `op=open name='default'` | 共享具名槽 `default`（此后该会话固定用它） |
| `defaultSpace: 'default'`（配置项改成具名） | 所有会话默认都用 `default`（退回旧行为，全局生效） |
| 无 session 的调用（`__global__`） | `default`，保证向后兼容 |

- **`defaultSpace`（A）**：volatile 标量，**留空/缺失折叠为 `:auto`**（1.6.0 起，此前折叠为 `default`），热更新不重注册。注意区分两个概念：配置值 `cfg.defaultSpace`（schema 里那个，可以是 `:auto` 或具名）与运行时**当前会话活值** `cfg.activeSpace`（命令实际用的 `useSpace(...)` 入参）；前者是设置，后者随会话与显式选择切换。
- **`:auto` 派生（C）**：`:auto` 在**两种模式**下都派生 `dsh-agent-<sid8>` —— 空间**命名**与 `isolateSpaces`（那个只管 Profile 落盘还是内存沙箱）是两条独立的轴。会话 id 会先剥掉 `session-` 前缀再取 8 位：真实 DSH id 形如 `session-52adc205-…`，直接 `slice(0,8)` 会得到 `session-`，让**所有会话撞成同一个空间**——这正是隔离失效的经典坑，已用 `sessionSpaceToken()` 修掉并有回归测试。
- **会话级隔离（B）**：活动空间追踪器按 `sessionId` 键控成一张槽位表（`Map<string,Slot>`，无 session 的调用落 `__global__` 槽保持向后兼容）。每个 `bcdp_*` 调用一进来就 `setCurrentSession(callingSessionId(exec))`，所以**并发多会话各开各的空间互不漂移**——A 会话重启空间不波及 B。
- **不要再手动建编号空间**：不需要 `#4`/`#5` 这类手工命名，隔离已经由会话派生自动完成；需要共享就走显式 `default`。

### 跨调用稳定定位（D1）

`bcdp_snapshot` 现在带稳定 locator：输出里每个可交互节点除了 `[ref=N]` 还附 `loc=css:…` / `loc=role:…` / `loc:href:…`。**跨调用请优先用 `loc=` 而非 `@N`**——`@N` 每次快照重新编号且其 ref 映射只活在取快照的那个子进程里，而 `loc=` 稳定、能跨子进程命中（`bcdp_click` / `bcdp_fill` 直接吃 `loc=...`）。这是插件层解法，未改内置运行时 SDK 的 ref 编号生成。

### navigate 卡死自愈（F）

`bcdp_navigate` 包了一层 watchdog：当一次导航因页面主线程挂死而 eval 超时 / `no active tab` 时，先**开一个空白 tab 再关掉挂死那个**（顺序关键：先关会触发末-tab 守卫留下死 tab），然后重试一次，结果附 `recoveredFrom`（正常路径为 `null`）。重试**硬上限一次**，二次仍卡如实返回，不用反复换 tab 掩盖真错误。

## 观察窗怎么用

右下角 **🌐 常驻小球** → 点开：

- **主画面**：agent 当前页面实况；点击/拖动/滚轮直接操作页面，Ctrl+滚轮缩放视图、Ctrl+拖动平移，双击复位。点击画面后可直接键盘输入，支持中文 IME、粘贴、Tab/Enter/方向键及 Ctrl/Cmd 快捷键。
- **选择元素**（点选引用）：点一下工具条进入点选模式，再点实时画面里的任意元素——插件捕获其 `backendNodeId`/`tag`/`id` 与语义描述，以 `[CDP-PICKS]` 结构化块并入对话输入框草稿；同一页面的多次点选自动合并进同一块并依次编号，agent 按编号精确取用。浮动观察球与侧边栏 Tab 均可用。
- **整页锚点报告**（@引用）：侧栏/历史抽屉里每个 tab 项的 `@` 按钮——一次点击抓取该页全部可交互元素（role+name+快照作用域 `sb-<anchor>`），归档为一份 `@"picks/*.json"` 整页报告投进输入框，让 agent 一眼拿到当前页面上下文而无需逐元素点选。同页二次点击覆盖刷新。这是 tab 粒度的快捷引用，与逐元素点选互补。
- **标签页条**：顶部横排，点选切换，`×` 关闭。
- **历史抽屉**（🕘）：按时间回看访问轨迹。
- 操作时下方网址行就地显示提示，2 秒后恢复。
- 面板关闭、sidebar Tab 隐藏或组件卸载后，1.5 秒宽限结束即停止画面生产。仅把 DSH 窗口切到后台不会停止串流，避免回前台时反复重建 WGC/FFmpeg；异常关闭由 120 秒 worker lease 超时兜底。

### 画面后端

- `cdp`：`Page.startScreencast` JPEG，默认 20 FPS。每个源帧立即按 Chrome 提供的帧 ID ACK，只保留最新待发帧；仅捕获当前观看标签，静态页恢复截图默认 3 秒一次。
- `ffmpeg`：Windows 以 `gfxcapture(hwnd)` 直接采集目标 Chrome 窗口的 D3D11 surface；其他平台使用显示来源 crop。随后编码 H.264 fragmented MP4 → HTTP 二进制 chunk → MediaSource `<video>`，不经过 Base64/SSE。
- `auto`：默认选择 CDP，不检测成功也不会自动下载 FFmpeg。FFmpeg 安装并通过能力检查后才可选择；已保存的 FFmpeg 后端若后来失效，本次观察会回退 CDP 并展示原因。
- **非 CDP 连接模式（本机 ego CLI / 本机 Tabbit CLI）**：这两类通道拿不到 `Page.startScreencast` 直推，观察窗改走**后台轮询拍帧**——每 3s 一次，帧写到临时文件后由 host 读回再广播（回执只带路径，不带字节）。因此它是“看快照”而不是“看直播”：静态页约 3s 一帧，重页面（单帧接近 8s 截止线）会明显低于这个频率；拿不到帧时以 `skipped` 标记跳过，不会挂死面板。
- Windows FFmpeg 必须包含 `gfxcapture`。插件按 browser PID、target title 和 CDP window bounds 匹配 HWND；窗口移动或被遮挡时仍捕获目标页面，并且不允许回退到桌面录制。若 target 是同一 Chrome 窗口里的后台 tab，会明确报错而不是展示当前可见 tab 或抢用户焦点。macOS 首次使用需要“屏幕录制”权限；X11 需要 Chromium 与 FFmpeg 共享 `DISPLAY`；Wayland 缺少 Portal/PipeWire 输入时会提示切回 CDP。

托管 FFmpeg 安装到 `~/.dsh/cache/ego-browser/ffmpeg/`，不会写入插件目录。Windows/Linux 使用固定 BtbN release tag；macOS 使用固定的 `ffmpeg-static` GitHub release 资产（其 Intel/Apple Silicon 二进制分别来源于 Evermeet/OSXExperts）。所有下载均固定资源 SHA-256，只提取 FFmpeg 主程序，不安装 `ffprobe` 或 `ffplay`。Windows/Linux 解包使用系统 `tar`；缺少时会在下载前明确报错。

> 登录态说明：多任务空间 Cookie 相互隔离，请在对应空间内登录。重启 DSH 后运行期登录态被清空（Chrome 运行期 Cookie 仅优雅关闭时落盘），需重登——扫码很快。

## 工作原理

- **工具层**：每个工具把参数拼成 JS 脚本，经 `ctx.subprocess` 用 `ego-browser nodejs` 喂给 stdin 运行，宿主经 CDP 驱动共享 Chromium。结果以 `@@DSH_RESULT@@` 哨兵行解析。所有 `bcdp_*` 经进程内互斥锁串行化，错误统一归一。激活项是本机 Tabbit CLI 时走分发器 `dispatchTabbit`：参数拼成 Playwright 片段经 `tabbit-cli nodejs` 执行，不复用 ego 子进程路径，也不得落到内置运行时。
- **观察窗**：`lib/client.js` 管理 watcher lease、JPEG `<img>` 与 MSE `<video>`；`lib/cast-server.js` 代理元数据 SSE、watch API 和带背压的二进制视频；worker 中 `CaptureManager` 保证同时只有一个活动后端和一个当前 target。CDP 控制面（标签、viewport、输入、验证码）独立于画面后端。

## JEV 风格管道：让 LLM 把控浏览器循环（阶段 10）

把"一帧 ≡ 截图 + 编号 DOM + 意图 + 操作进度"这个**帧契约**，连同"判定只回编号、绝不给选择器"的**判定接缝**，落地成一套可跑、可测、可归档的管道。判定由外部的 **Laya / JEV** 判定服务承担（见下），循环由本插件驱动。

**四个工具**（宿主侧 `defineTool`，判定请求从插件进程发 HTTP，不经过 agent 会话）：

| 工具 | 干什么 | 何时用 |
|---|---|---|
| `bcdp_jev_status` | **先跑这个**：判定链可用性 + 配置体检，**不发任何请求** | 怀疑配置/链路问题时第一步 |
| `bcdp_jev_frame` | 采一帧（截图 + 编号候选 + 意图），看判定器会看到什么 | 调试帧内容、核对候选编号 |
| `bcdp_jev_ask` | 组装请求体；`dryRun` 默认 true，可指定 `round=control\|chapter\|pick\|evaluate` 逐级看，确认无误再发 | 想先看清楚判定请求再发 |
| `bcdp_jev_run` | 跑整条循环，返回逐步 trace（每步的候选数 / top / 预算 / 命中） | 真要让它动手 |

**默认链路是 `laya → rule`**。JEV 目前无法注册，所以默认不写它；将来可用时把 `jev` 加回 `judgePrefer` 跳序并填 `jevUrl` 即可。`bcdp_jev_status` 在缺 key 时会主动打印本地起法（`ENGINE=laya … uvicorn laya_api.main:app`，端口 **8000** 而非 7789，`ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=true` 建 key）。不可用的跳**跳过不调用**（laya 强制鉴权无匿名分支，缺 key 必然 401），每一跳的跳过与失败都进 trace，绝不静默回落；`refuse` 是结果不是异常。

**三级缩小（让 LLM 把控进程，而不是一次猜全部）**：
1. `control` —— 要不要动手（固定 5 项：`pick_button` / `sleep` / `next` / `prev` / `done`）；
2. `chapter` —— 哪个章节（按 AX 容器聚簇，从 `childIds` 父链挑最近的结构化祖先，如 `form#1` / `form#2`；单章节时此轮跳过）；
3. `pick` —— 章节内选哪个编号 + 一个风险度 `score`。

分章节不是装饰：阈值按候选数分桶，**把 20 选 1 拆成「几选 1 × 几选 1」会让两轮都落进更严的桶**（`top≥0.5` 且 `top−second≥0.15`），比一次性 20 选 1（`top≥0.6`）更可控。判定器**只回编号**，坐标/选择器由执行层每次重新量（`DOM.getBoxModel` + 点击前 `DOM.getNodeForLocation` 命中复核），帧里的矩形绝不作为点击依据。

**判定上下文是隔离的**：只允许 `INTENT` / `PROGRESS` / `FRAME` / `HISTORY` 四段，**绝不带 agent 会话 session 前缀**；多出任何一段都在组装时直接抛错（不靠约定，靠断言）。`PROGRESS`（步数 / 各章节尝试与结果 / 真正成功过的动作 / 剩余预算）由循环自己**机械生成**，不让模型写——模型写的进度是第二难发现的幻觉通道。

**评估开关 `jevEvaluate`（默认开，设置面板可关）**：每一步执行后，判定器再判一遍进度是 `inprogress` / `done` / `fail`。`fail` 或「未验真的 done」不猜下一步，而是**升级为 `escalate`**——带一组有序的 `RecoveryOption`（如先 `reload` 刷新，因为陈旧渲染会藏住已写入的确认），交回 LLM 决定恢复还是停手。

**循环终止态**：`done`（对照 `successCriteria` 自验）/ `blocked`（预算拦）/ `exhausted`（预算耗尽，带 `exhaustedKind`）/ `stuck`（同锚同动作连续 3 次无变化）/ `unavailable`（无判定器）/ `error` / `escalate`。

> 现状诚实记录：本阶段已证明**协议、阈值、终止、分章节、组装、隔离**正确（`bcdp_jev_*` 单测覆盖），但**尚未在真实浏览器上端到端跑过**（T10.22 待做）；判定**准确率**未经实测（阈值分桶是标定用的，不是选得对的证明）。存档的被操作元素会保留 `class` 等定位特征（只剥离检视器外壳 token），供 escalate 时回传给 LLM 恢复。

## 开发

源码在 `src/`（TypeScript），构建产物在 `lib/`（host + client bundle）与 `bin/cdp-cast-worker.mjs`（worker bundle）。

```sh
pnpm typecheck   # tsc 类型门禁（tsconfig.json 主 + tsconfig.client.json 客户端）
pnpm test        # vitest 单元测试
pnpm run build   # tsdown 三 bundle：lib/index.js + lib/client.js + bin/cdp-cast-worker.mjs
```

> 直接改 `src/`（`src/index.ts` 工具层、`src/client/index.ts` 前端、`src/worker/cdp-cast-worker.ts` worker）。新工具在 `registerActionTools` 里按 `t({...})` 加，并在 `bcdp_help` 索引（`src/help.ts`）补一条，跑 `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm run build`。`lib/` 与 `bin/cdp-cast-worker.mjs` 是构建产物（预构建入库），不要手改。

`node_modules/` 仅含指向 DSH checkout 的符号链接（编译期类型解析）；运行时由 harness 解析 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`。

## 已知限制（诚实说明）

- **Windows**：插件层已做 v0.4.0 适配；内置运行时的宿主对 Windows 仍以社区适配为主，复杂多步流程稳定性可能弱于 macOS。
- **FFmpeg 平台捕获**：Windows 已使用 `gfxcapture(HWND)`，需要包含该 filter 的新构建；PATH 中的旧 FFmpeg 会被跳过并提示下载兼容版本。Linux 使用 `x11grab`、macOS 使用 `avfoundation` display crop；macOS ScreenCaptureKit、Wayland Portal helper 属后续增强。
- **安装环境**：本仓库的 DSH peer 包不全在公共 npm registry。普通 `pnpm install` 可能在解析 `@deepseek-ai/*` peer 时失败；DSH profile 安装应提供这些 peer。CDP 不依赖 FFmpeg，也不会在插件安装阶段下载二进制。
- **快照质量**：Linux 用 CDP `DOMSnapshot` 重建语义树，非 macOS 内核级，复杂 iframe/画布场景可能降级。
- **宿主可靠性（Linux）**：未合并的社区 PR，跨 CLI 调用间可能丢 tab/空间状态；插件已内置防御，简单流程稳定，复杂流程可能需重试。
- **登录态持久化**：Chrome 运行期 Cookie 仅优雅关闭时落盘，强杀重启需重登。
- **Tabbit 通道覆盖面**：仅 `space` / `navigate` / `snapshot` / `click` / `fill` / `screenshot` / `tab op=list` 已接入，其余工具返回明确错误而不回落其他后端；观察窗只能看帧、不能点选元素引用，无下载事件（`capabilities.ts` 的 `tabbit` 投影：`overlay` / `bindingCalled` / `downloadEvents` / `browserClose` 均为 false）。`bcdp_jev_*` 评审链在 Tabbit 下没有接入分发器，调用返回“尚未支持”而不是错驱另一个浏览器。
- 输出 schema 为宽松 `additionalProperties: true`，客户端以实际返回值为准。

插件本体 MIT。内置运行时嵌入第三方 MIT 代码；可选下载的 FFmpeg 构建涉及 GPL-3.0-or-later 义务。使用或再分发前请阅读构建来源的许可证与源码获取信息，来源与署名详见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-browser-cdp/blob/HEAD/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。

## 供应链与权限说明

为目录收录与审查提供的确定性事实：

- **运行文件**：`lib/`（构建产物，由 `npm run build` 从 `src/` TypeScript 以 tsdown 确定性生成）、`bin/`（worker 与 ffmpeg-probe 的可执行入口脚本）、`cordis.patch.yml`（装配层）、`dsh-plugin.json`（manifest）。`*.map` 仅为调试用 sourcemap，不参与运行，已声明排除。
- **原生/可执行工件**：`runtime/` 内置 ego 兼容运行时（第三方 MIT，来源与逐文件清单见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-browser-cdp/blob/HEAD/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)）——它是本插件的核心功能（自带受管 Chrome/CDP 宿主），属有意携带的可执行工件，非构建副产物。`runtime/PATCHES.md` 记录对内置运行时的全部本地补丁。
- **依赖**：运行时依赖仅 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（由 DSH 宿主提供对等实现）；peer 依赖全部为 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 宿主服务。客户端 bundle 的外部模块由宿主模块表解析，不携带 npm 运行时依赖。
- **外部服务**：无遥测、无外部 API 调用。唯一的网络行为是**可选的** FFmpeg 安装器按用户指令从 GitHub（或用户配置的镜像）下载构建件，来源校验与许可义务见 [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-browser-cdp/blob/HEAD/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。
- **失败边界**：宿主无 webServer（TUI/headless）时 watch 路由安全跳过；worker 启动失败时 watch 路由返回 `ok:false` 的 JSON 而非挂起；浏览器进程随宿主 teardown 一并终止（`--stop` fire-and-forget，不阻塞宿主退出）。
- **权限**：manifest `permissions` 为空——工具集的文件读写被限定在 ego 自管的空间目录与用户工作区，网络访问经由受管的 agent 浏览器而非宿主进程。

# dsh-tg-bridge

Drive [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com) from Telegram. It runs on the
machine that already has the harness, and it answers in the chat where you asked.

A forum topic is a project: its own session, working directory, model,
permissions and language. Two topics share the install and nothing else.

Never made a bot? [QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/HEAD/QUICKSTART.md) goes from "no account" to a bot
that answers, one step at a time.

## What it does

- **A model per topic.** `/model` lists the routes the profile declares — provider
  and model together — and a tap switches this topic only. `/model <route> all`
  moves the default the other topics follow; `/model auto` hands the topic back.
  A chat for thinking out loud and a chat for engineering no longer share one model.
- **A topic is a project.** `/cd my-app`, and every turn runs from that directory —
  on a permission-enabled profile the sandbox is narrowed to it too, so the agent
  cannot write outside the project.
- **One edited message per turn.** Steps, a timer and the cache hit rate, plus the
  reasoning in a collapsed block you can tap open. A long turn adds a second
  collapsed block with every tool call. `/stop` is a button on that message.
- **`/diff` — review the turn, one hunk at a time.** The working tree is split into
  files and hunks; every hunk gets two buttons: explain it, or revert just that
  hunk. A button carries a hash of the hunk it was drawn from, so a press that
  arrives after the file moved on is refused instead of touching a line nobody was
  looking at. `/diff stat` is the file list alone.
- **An endpoint from the chat.** `/endpoint add   
  [model,model]` writes the provider without an AI turn, and the key itself is
  never typed — only the name of the variable that holds it. The new models appear
  on `/model` as routes.
- **Input: text, voice, photos.** Any speech engine plugs in — a local script, any
  command-line tool, or an OpenAI-compatible API (see [`docs/VOICE.md`](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/HEAD/docs/VOICE.md))
  — and the transcript is shown before the answer. A photo is read by the turn's own
  model through `read_image`, text and UI included; no second model is needed.
- **Goal and checklist per topic.** `/goal`, `/tasks`; both survive restarts and
  are prepended to every turn.
- **Two scopes for every setting.** `/reasoning <mode> all` moves the default,
  without `all` it moves this topic; language and pinning follow the same rule,
  and `/crew use reviewer` gives one topic its own effort, permissions and agent
  preset (four built-in sets, read-only, copyable).
- **It says what it cost.** A turn reports tokens and the cache hit rate; `/cost`
  says what the session has spent and `/prices` shows the rates it used.
- **Out of quota is not a dead end.** When the quota runs out it switches to a
  free model right away, and the answer says which route answered.
- **No lost messages.** A journal with acknowledgement and replay.
- **Knows how busy the computer is.** `/load` shows free space on the topic's disk,
  free RAM and average CPU, plus how many turns are running and waiting. `/load on`
  makes a prompt wait instead of starting while the machine is over a limit you set
  — kept, never refused, and one press sends it anyway.
- **Languages.** Menus and service messages in `en`, `ru`, `zh`; `/lang` pins the
  topic language, and without it a new topic takes the language of the message
  itself (Cyrillic → `ru`, Han characters → `zh`), then the Telegram
  `language_code`, then `en`.
- **"Stop" / "Retry" buttons and tool confirmations** sit in the message, so there
  is no command to type to stop a run.
- **`/report`.** One command turns "it broke" into a redacted document: version,
  profile, preset, model, directory, the last failure and the log tail, with keys
  and home paths removed before the file is written.
- **`dsh-tg check`.** Diagnostics in one command, changing nothing on the system.

## First run

`setup.mjs` leaves a working bridge with these defaults, and none of them need
a decision before the first message:

| Setting | Default | Where to change it |
|---|---|---|
| profile | `headless` | `/profile` |
| folder | the workspace you ran setup in | `/cd` |
| idle limit | 2 minutes without output stops the turn | `/settings` |
| hard ceiling | none — a long turn runs until it ends | `/settings` |
| parallel turns | 3 | `/settings` |
| plain text | off (Markdown answers) | `/settings` |
| model fallback | on, empty chain | `/fallback` |
| voice messages | off | `/voice` |
| topic log | on | `/settings` |
| command menu | installed for this bot | `node bot-menu.mjs` |

The first three commands are enough to be productive: `/cd <project>` binds the
topic to a folder, `/model` picks the model with buttons, `/menu` is every
command as a card, grouped. `/start` answers with the same three and offers a five-step tour — folder, model, files, the turn and the way back, the switches — each step naming one command as a button; `/help`
explains any command in one message; `/settings` holds the switches above.

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 24 (the version DeepSeek Harness ships; sessions are zstd-compressed)
- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer in the `0.2.x` line (`>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`)
- DeepSeek Harness installed (`~/.dsh/profiles/headless`)
- A Telegram bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)

The supported harness range is declared in `engines.dsh`; that field decides
compatibility on its own (DSH ignores `peerDependencies` when it is present).
The range includes an explicit prerelease branch, because a plain `<0.3.0`
silently excludes `0.2.2-*` builds. A future `0.3.0` needs an explicit bump:
the bridge relies on the `0.2.x` CLI flags and profile layout.

## Ecosystem

The Chinese DSH community maintains the largest plugin catalogs and the
in-app markets that read them; this bridge follows their packaging rules so it
can be listed next to them:

- [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) — bilingual (English /
  中文) plugin list and the `dsh-plugin-catalog` npm package
- [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — the Chinese-built
  in-app market with one-click install and themes
- [dsh-find-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/dsh-find-plugin) —
  finds a plugin from chat instead of browsing a catalog

## Languages

- Menus (`/` in chat): three sets, `ru` by default, plus `en` and `zh`; a client whose locale matches neither gets the Russian set.
- Topic language: `/lang en|ru|zh`; stored in `state.json` and survives a restart.
- A new user gets the language from the Telegram `language_code`; anything that is not `ru`/`zh` → `en`.
- Translated so far: menus, the start message, turn status, errors, `/cd`, `/new`, `/stop`, `/lang`,
  the reply to an unknown command. Long reports (`/status`, `/sessions`, `/model` and similar)
  are still in Russian, that is the next pass.

## Installation

One command: your bot token and your numeric id. Nothing to edit by hand.

**Windows, macOS or Linux — Node.js 24 or newer.** `init` and the bridge run
anywhere; `setup` (stop, autostart, restart) is **Windows-only** today, so on
macOS and Linux use `sh install.sh`, which registers `launchd` or `systemd --user`.
`node setup.mjs --check` reports state on every platform.

```bash
npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init --token 123456789:AA... --user 123456789
npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest setup
```

`init` writes the token, your id and the working directory; `setup` registers
autostart and starts the bridge.

### What it needs from DSH

The bridge is a client of the DSH CLI, and the surface it uses is small enough to
write down: `--profile`, `--json`, `--session-id`, `--expose-internals <cli.js>`
when the app binary runs the CLI, and the `{"type": ...}` JSON events on stdout.
Profiles are read as files (`cordis.patch.yml`, `package.json`) under
`~/.dsh/profiles`. `package.json` spells the supported range out in
`engines.dsh`, and it is capped below `0.3.0` on purpose: a minor bump may rename
an event, and a bridge that guesses is a bridge that answers with silence.

Two escape hatches, for a moved app or a DSH that ships differently:

```bash
DSH_BIN=/usr/local/bin/dsh        # the CLI itself, no entrypoint argument
DSH_CLI_JS=/opt/dsh/lib/cli.js    # just the CLI entrypoint, run by DSH_BIN
DSH_APP_DIR=/opt/DeepSeek-Harness # where the desktop app is installed
```

`/doctor` prints the command a turn would actually run, so a machine where these
matter says so instead of failing with an empty answer.

**As a DSH plugin** (the package carries a `dsh.bundle`; the catalog entry is
pending review):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-tg-bridge
```

The plugin starts one bridge when DSH boots and stops it on shutdown; if a
bridge is already running (for example from the scheduled task), it leaves it
alone. Run `npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init ...` first so a config exists.

What `init` does:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| bot token | `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` → `refs.DSH_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`; other keys are left alone |
| your id and working directory | `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/config.json`; an existing file is not overwritten |
| `headless` profile | checked, with a hint on how to create it if missing |

`init` flags: `--cwd <path>` (default `~/Projects`), `--voice` (enable
voice transcription), `--dry-run` (show what would be written, change nothing).

Optional provider settings live in `config.json`:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `providerKeys` | extra env var names to pass to a turn, read from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`; default `[]` |
| `pricesUrl` | retired: `/prices` always reads OpenRouter's public list and labels the number as a reference for the model |
| `vision.patch` | opt-in overlay profile for photo turns; default `""` — the turn's own model reads images |
| `vision.enabled` | set `true` to run photo turns on `vision.patch` instead of the topic profile |
| `fallbackModels` | ordered failover chain; default `[]` — see below |
| `fallbackEnabled` | `false` switches the whole chain off without editing the list; `/fallback off` sets it |
| `maxParallel` | how many topics run at once, 1–8, default `3`; also `/jobs 5` in the chat |
| `replayWindowMs` | how old a journaled update may be and still be replayed after a restart; default `600000` (10 min) |

Each `fallbackModels` entry is one attempt, tried in order after the turn's own
model refuses:

```json
{
  "provider": "router-a",
  "model": "some-model",
  "patch": "~/.dsh/tg-bridge/model-a.yml",
  "free": false,
  "off": false
}
```

`patch` is an overlay file with a single `agent-default-model` row
(`provider` + `model`); it is materialised once as its own profile, so the turn
keeps every other setting and only the model changes. `provider` is the id the
provider is written under in the profile — it decides whose key and host the
pre-flight probe asks, so the same model id on two routers stays two attempts.
`free` only adds `(free)` to the switch notice. `off` keeps an entry in the list
but out of the walk; an entry whose `patch` file is missing is skipped the same
way, and the chat says so instead of counting it.

The chain may mix companies: a 503 from one provider says nothing about another,
so a busy channel skips its own models and the next company is still tried. Put
models from different companies next to each other — two arms of one router are
one outage, not two chances — and keep the `:free` models at the end, as the
last resort.

**What starts a switch.** Anything the provider itself says no to: a 400/413/422
refusal (its own validator rejecting the request), 401/403 (key refused), 402 or
a quota/balance message (empty account), 404 (that model id is not carried),
429 (rate limit), 5xx and `get_channel_failed` / "all providers busy" (the pool
is down), a dropped connection or DNS/TLS failure, and an empty answer. A refusal
gets one other route, not the whole chain: it is replayed in full, and if the
second vendor refuses identically the request — not the route — is what is wrong,
so the reply says to start a fresh session with `/new`.

**What does not start a switch.** The turn time cap, `/stop`, a session or
directory error, a missing `dsh` binary: no other vendor changes those, and a
replay would cost a full turn to learn the same thing. They are listed in the
card so the distinction is visible instead of guessed.

### `/fallback` — the chain from the chat

```
/fallback                 the card: chain state, numbered routes, what starts a switch
/fallback on | off        the whole chain (per route: /fallback off 3)
/fallback use 3 | skip 3  one route back in or out
/fallback up 3 | down 3   move a route in the order
/fallback test [3]        ask each route (or one) with a 1-token request
/fallback add <provider>/<model>     write an overlay and append the route
/fallback first <provider>/<model>   put it at the head: tried before every other route
/fallback remove 3        drop a route from the list (its overlay file stays)
```

Every line has a button on the card: `● n` switches a route, `↑ n` / `↓ n` move
it, and the card redraws in place after each press. `test` proves the key and the
channel are alive — not that the provider accepts this conversation, so a route
can answer `ping` and still refuse a long prompt with a 400. The card says that
in as many words.

`test` also times each route: how long it takes to produce the first token, and
which live route is fastest right now. Two routes that both answer are not
equally good — 400 ms and 9 s feel like different products — and the head of the
chain is the one a person picks on that number. A route that did not answer
prints no time, so `no balance · 120 ms` can never read as "works, just slow".

`first` exists because `add` appends: when the route you want should answer
*before* the primary, appending it means moving it up eight times and guessing
where the head is. `/fallback first router-a/deepseek-v4.1-flash` writes the
same overlay and puts it at position 1 — or moves it there if it is already in
the chain.

Get your id from [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot), the token from
[@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather).

### Bot settings in Telegram

Three things without which the bot will stay silent in a group or work only halfway:

1. **Privacy mode → Disable** (`/setprivacy` in BotFather). Otherwise the bot sees
   only commands, not regular text in a topic.
2. **Topics enabled** in the group settings (Edit → Topics). Without them all work
   goes to a single chat and per-topic sessions are not created.
3. **Pin Messages** permission for the bot. Only needed to pin the first
   message of a topic; without it the bridge keeps working but will not pin.

You do not need to set up the command menu by hand: `init` and `setup` install it
in Russian, English and Chinese at once. The menu is not refreshed by a plain
bridge restart, so after adding commands run `dsh-tg menu`. The full settings
table, permissions, checks and common errors are in
[docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md).

**Autostart** has two routes. `sh install.sh` writes `launchd` on macOS and
`systemd --user` on Linux; `dsh-tg setup` registers the `DSH-TG-Bridge` task on
Windows, which runs the guarded supervisor (the same launcher on logon and every
five minutes) so a crashed bridge comes back without a second poller. On macOS
and Linux `setup` declines and names `install.sh`, because it stops the old
bridge with `taskkill` and registers autostart through `schtasks`.

**Manual install** (if you want full control):

```bash
npm install -g dsh-tg-bridge
dsh-tg init --token 123456789:AA... --user 123456789
dsh-tg check     # report only, changes nothing
dsh-tg setup     # stop the old bridge and start the new one
```

If the bridge is already installed, `setup` restarts it on the new code and reinstalls
the command menu.

## Troubleshooting

Starting from nothing, or helping someone who is: [QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/HEAD/QUICKSTART.md)
has the same answers with the terminal output they will actually see.

Error replies end with a code, which tells you what to fix:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA` | provider balance is empty: top up or stay on free models (`/prices`, `/model`) |
| `TG_CONFLICT` | a second process is polling the same bot: `/doctor`, then `/restart` |
| `TG_POLL` | Telegram did not answer a long poll inside its own clock. The bridge retried by itself; one line is nothing, a run of them for minutes is VPN/DNS or a route that died |
| `TG_NET` | no network to Telegram at all: the bridge keeps retrying, nothing was lost |
| `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` | no provider key in the profile: add it in the DSH app |
| `NO_DSH_CLI` | DeepSeek Harness CLI not found: check the app installation |
| `NETWORK` | no network to the provider: retry, check VPN/DNS |
| `SANDBOX_DENY` | DSH denied access to a file or directory: check the project path and permissions |
| `UNKNOWN_MODEL` | the model from the config is unavailable: `/model` lists the working ones |
| `EMPTY_RESPONSE` | the model returned nothing: retry or switch model (`/model`) |
| `TURN_TIME_CAP` | the turn hit its own time ceiling: the work is saved, press Continue |
| `TURN_FAILED` | cause not recognized: `/doctor` and `/logs errors` |

### Lines in the bridge log

Not every line is an error, and the ones that are usually name their own cause.
These are the phrases people actually ask about — the first word of each is what
to search for in `/logs`:

| The line | What happened | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `poll error [TG_POLL]: The operation was aborted due to timeout — retry in 5s` | Telegram held the long poll past its own timeout. The bridge dropped it and asked again, which is the normal way to poll | nothing, if it is one line; if it repeats for minutes, check VPN/DNS |
| `poll error [TG_NET]: fetch failed` | no route to Telegram | it keeps retrying; fix the network |
| `Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request` | two processes poll the same token — a second bridge, or `dsh web` started its own | `/doctor` shows the pid; `/restart confirm` or stop the other copy |
| `no activity for 2 min — turn interrupted` | the model went silent past the idle limit; the turn was stopped | `/stop` if it is still marked busy, then resend. `/settings` moves the limit |
| `the CLI exited with code 1 and printed nothing` | DSH itself did not start, so the turn never existed | `/doctor`, then `/logs errors`; `/dsh` shows the installed version |
| `[DSH] is not at <path>` | the topic's profile points at a path with no DSH | install DSH, or `/dsh` for the check |
| `could not start the DSH turn` | spawn failed — permissions, disk, antivirus | the message carries the system reason |
| `The button failed — /logs errors has the reason` | the card outlived the state it pointed at, usually after a restart | `/menu` draws a fresh card |
| `the provider cut the request off at its own 60-second ceiling` | the provider closed the stream, not the bridge | the fallback chain takes over; `/fallback` shows it |
| `turn ended without an answer` | the stream finished with no text and no error | retry; if it repeats, `/model` another route |

A turn that fails on purpose says so in words — "the sandbox refused", "the
provider ran out of its own clock" — because a person reading it is deciding
what to do next, not debugging.

## Checks

Send the bot:

| Command | Expected |
|---|---|
| `/doctor` | report: pid, Telegram, disk, directory, session |
| `/update` | which bridge runs, what npm has, and whether a newer release exists (`/update confirm` installs it) |
| `/thoughts [file\|all\|off]` | the last turn's reasoning as a message; `file`/`all` send the full log as a Markdown document, `off` hides the block |
| `/help` | commands grouped by category |
| `/cd my-app` | topic bound to the project, and the sandbox narrowed to it |
| `/diff [stat]` | what the turn changed, one hunk at a time: every hunk has "explain" and "revert this hunk"; a stale button is refused |
| `/find <text> [path]` | where a literal string lives in the topic's folder: matches as buttons that open the file at the matched line; binary and oversized files are skipped and counted |
| `/report` | a redacted bundle (version, profile, preset, model, cwd, last failure, log tail) sent to the owner as a document; in a group, the path only |
| `/prices` | what the current model costs, and whose price that is: your provider's, the same model on another gateway, or "no public price" when nobody publishes one |

### Settings as a card

`/settings` draws the same switches that the commands set, in one message with
four tabs: what the bot says, who answers and how hard it works, new releases,
and the health checks. Each row shows what the setting is now and what a tap
would change it to. A tap runs the command a person would have typed
(`/reasoning chat`, `/update on`), so the card cannot disagree with the command:
it is a view of them.

The card stays after a tap. It is edited in place — same message, same buttons,
the value in force marked with `●` and one `✓ row: value` line saying what just
changed — so a second setting is one more tap instead of a second `/settings`.
`✓ Done` removes the card when you are finished with it; nothing else deletes it.

`📌 Pin the progress card` (`/pin on`) keeps the running card pinned, so the
clock, the speed and the step list are one tap away instead of a scroll. Telegram
gives a chat one pinned message, so each turn's card replaces the last one. Off by
default: a bot that pins without being asked takes that slot in someone else's
chat, and a group needs the right to pin at all.

Nothing on the card is only available on the card. `/settings` is for people who
would rather press a labelled button than remember which of `/effort`,
`/preset` and `/crew` changes what.

Every command answers `/help` in the chat, in the language you write in: a
message written in Cyrillic or Han characters switches the topic to Russian or
Chinese even when the phone's menu is set to another language, and `/lang`
pins a choice above that. The Telegram menu shows the same list, minus
`/subscribe`: it is one line, and a person who turns it off should not have to
find it in a menu again.

## Updates

The npm tag `latest` is a label, not an updater: installing a package pins the
version on disk, and nothing moves until something moves it. Two switches, both
about this install (not about a topic, because it is the install that updates):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/update` | one line: what runs here, what is published, which switches are set |
| `/update on` | tell me about new releases: one message per version, checked once a day |
| `/update off` | stop telling me; nothing installs, nothing moves |
| `/update auto` | besides telling me, install the release by itself (checked hourly) |
| `/update confirm` | install the new release now, by hand |

Nothing above installs except `confirm` and `auto`, and even those only change the
files: the running process keeps its old modules until `/restart confirm`, so a
bad release never lands mid-chat. `confirm` and `auto` copy the replaced files to
`update-backup-<date>` and print the path; copying that folder back is the way to
roll back, with no state to undo.

`/subscribe on|off` says the same thing as `/update on|off`, for people who do not
want to read `/update` first. It is not in the Telegram menu on purpose.

There are no notices about failures. The bridge cannot decide what counts as one
for you, and "something failed" that nobody can act on is noise; errors stay in
the chat where they happened, under `/doctor` and `/logs errors`.

## How it works

```
Telegram → bridge.mjs → dsh --profile headless --json → reply
             │
             ├─ pending/ journal + ack  (messages are not lost)
             ├─ per-topic queue         (turns in topics run in parallel)
             ├─ progress + buttons      (you can see the work is going)
             └─ fail-fast on quota      (free models as a fallback)
```

The bridge is a single process with long polling. Each turn spawns a separate
CLI process that exits after the answer, so "no DSH process" between
turns is normal, not a failure.

### Steering during a turn

If you write in a topic while a turn is still running, the message does not queue
behind it: the bridge drops the task into `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/steer/`, the `dsh-steer-inbox`
plugin hands it to the live agent on its next step, and the agent immediately replies with a short
line in the chat: what it is doing now and where it put the addition. If the agent stays silent
for 90 seconds, the bridge writes one neutral line itself so there is no silence.

Attachments work the same way. A voice note is transcribed first and its transcript is echoed in
the chat, then the text is steered into the running turn; a photo or a file is downloaded to a
local path and that path is steered, exactly as an idle turn would hand it over.

What each kind of attachment becomes inside a running turn:

| Sent | Inside the turn | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| voice note, audio file, audio sent as a document | transcript, echoed as `🎤 …` before the steer | any engine you point `voice` at: `script`, `command` or an OpenAI-compatible `openai` endpoint; **off by default** |
| small text file (`.md`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.py`, `.log`, … up to 60 KB) | the content itself between `<file>` markers — no tool call needed | nothing |
| PDF, archive, binary, anything bigger | its local path under `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/inbox/` | nothing; the agent opens it with its own tools |
| video, video note, animation | its path; the agent can pull frames or sound out with ffmpeg | ffmpeg, only if frames or audio are needed |
| photo | its path plus one honest line; the turn reads it with `read_image`, and says so in one line if it cannot | a model that accepts images |

Voice is the one row with a hidden prerequisite: something has to turn audio into
text. Faster-whisper is what `init --voice` writes, but it is not the only answer —
`voice.provider` also takes `command` (whisper.cpp, Vosk, a wrapper of your own) or
`openai` (OpenAI, Groq, a local server; anything that speaks
`/audio/transcriptions`). With no backend configured, a voice note is not swallowed:
the bridge says what is missing and points at [`docs/VOICE.md`](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/HEAD/docs/VOICE.md).

A caption does not turn the attachment into a text-only message: it is folded into the same
hand-over, so "why did this fail" plus a `.log` file arrives as one steer.

An album is one request, not ten. Telegram delivers it as one update per file, all sharing a
`media_group_id`; the bridge collects the group (1.2 s of quiet after the last item, at most
4 s) and hands it over once — one steer into a running turn, one turn when the topic is idle.

### When a turn hits the time ceiling

`turnTimeoutMs` (default 30 min, this install 75) is a ceiling, not a target: if a turn reaches
it, the bridge stops it with `⏱` instead of letting one runaway loop own the topic for hours.
Nothing is lost — the session and every file the turn produced stay in place — so the message
carries **⏵ Continue**, which asks the agent to check the state and go on from where it stopped.
That is deliberately not the same as **Retry**, which would redo the whole task from the start.

This needs the plugin from this repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add link:<path-to-repository>/plugin/steer-inbox
```

and a line in `~/.dsh/profiles/headless/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: steer-inbox
      name: 'dsh-steer-inbox'
```

The bridge checks the profile itself: if the line is missing, it does not write the task
(it would just expire) and behaves as before, queueing the message.

### Live thoughts and reasoning

Two things land in the same progress message, and neither sends a chat message of its own.

**The model's reasoning.** Every `thinking` block the CLI commits is folded into one
Telegram `<blockquote expandable>`: collapsed it is a single line, tapped it opens the whole
trail of the turn, and it stays there after the turn ends — the same way the desktop app shows
a reasoning section you can expand. The block is written once, in the final edit of the turn,
and never touched again: Telegram re-collapses an expanded block on every edit of its message,
which used to yank the chat away from a half-read paragraph. While the turn runs the message
only gets a counter (`🧠 Размышления · 4821`) and the last three steps, so the live edits stay
short. Escaped, and trimmed to its tail when a turn thinks longer than a message can hold; the
panel never exceeds one message. A cut block says `… · начало скрыто · /thoughts file`, which
sends the whole log as a document. If the API refuses the markup, the same content is retried
as plain text.

**The steps.** Three calls fit inline. A turn that makes more moves its complete step list into
a second collapsed block, added in that same final edit, so "what did it actually run" is one
tap away instead of a count.

**The agent's own notes.** The agent can add a short decision trail:

```bash
node ~/.dsh/tg-bridge/say.mjs --thought "checking why the watchdog fired twice"
```

The note is appended to `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/thoughts/<chat>_<thread>.jsonl`; the progress
message shows the last two as `💭` lines. The command needs no ids: it falls back to the
newest turn's thought file, because tool shells do not inherit the bridge environment.
`--thought` sends a Telegram message of its own only in `/reasoning chat` mode.

A decision the person must know before the turn ends — a release shipped, a cause found,
a blocker — goes to the chat as one plain line instead:

```bash
node ~/.dsh/tg-bridge/say.mjs --note "1.10.1 is on npm; restart to load it"
```

`--note` sends a real message and takes the same no-ids fallback as `--thought`. The split
is deliberate: `--thought` is the working trail (inside the progress message, and in `chat`
mode also as its own messages), `--note` is the short line that changes what the reader
expects to happen next — useful in `card` and `off` mode, redundant in `chat`. The progress
message itself opens with the request echoed back (`⏳ Принял: «…» · 3 с`), so the first
thing the person sees after sending names their task rather than a generic spinner.

`/reasoning` is the switch for the 💭 mechanism, and it has three ends:

- `/reasoning card` (the default) — every turn carries a short instruction to leave one line
  at each decision point (task clear, cause found, risky change, result checked), and the
  progress message shows the last two;
- `/reasoning chat` — the same lines, each also posted as its own message, so a turn that
  runs for twenty minutes is read as it happens instead of scrolled back to afterwards.
  The prompt says so explicitly, so a line is written to stand alone;
- `/reasoning off` — drops the instruction and the `💭` lines for that topic, for when the
  step list is all you want.

A topic switched to `chat` mid-turn does not dump the steps already in the card: forwarding
starts with the next line written. The setting lives in `state.json` per topic, so a chatty
research topic and a terse deploy topic can differ; a `true`/`false` written by an older
release still reads as `card`/`off`. The settings card offers the same three ends as buttons.

The reasoning block itself is model output; `/thoughts` is what reads it back:

- `/thoughts` — the last turn as a message, in parts, deleted after three minutes;
- `/thoughts file` — the **whole** last turn as `reasoning-<date>-file.md`, sent as a document
  (a five-hour turn is tens of thousands of characters, which no chat message can hold);
- `/thoughts all` — every turn of the session in one file (a long session is a couple of MB);
- `/thoughts off` / `on` — keep the block out of the turn panel (the panel then shows
  `🧠 Размышления · N · /thoughts file`) or bring it back.

The log is built from the session file on demand, so nothing is duplicated while a turn runs.
Files land in `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/thoughts/` and older ones are pruned after a week.

### Profiles per topic

The desktop app lets you build several profiles for different kinds of work, each with its own
plugin set and model. The same switch works from a topic:

```
/profile                    current profile, available ones, hints
/profile research           run this topic's turns on another profile
/profile new research from web
                            create a profile from a shipped template and bind it
/profile default            back to the install default
```

A new profile is written by `dsh <name> --from-default-profile <template> --dump-config`, so
nothing boots and no plugin is loaded at creation time; dependencies are installed by the
profile's first turn. The binding is per topic: `/plugins` manages that profile's rows, and
`/plugins search <word>` lists what the npm registry
has with the `dsh-plugin` keyword — the desktop app's plugin browser, from the chat. Each result
carries a plus button that runs `/plugins add <name>`.

`/model` is a step finer than the binding. A topic that never chose a model boots the profile
it is bound to; `/model <route>` stores the route for that topic alone, and the next turn boots a
copy of the profile with the `agent-default-model` row rewritten — provider, model and the other
keys of that row, `reasoningEffort` included, carried over. The copy is rebuilt whenever the
profile changes, so a provider added to the profile reaches the topics that had already chosen.
`/model <route> all` writes the profile itself, and `/model auto` deletes the topic's route.

### The directory a topic writes in

`/cd my-app` does two things, and they are worth separating because they used to
be one: the turn runs *in* that directory, and the sandbox *stops* at it. The
second half only works on a profile that has a permission table — the bridge
writes the row only when one exists, and never invents one for a profile that
opted out.

```
/cd my-app            bind the topic: run here, and write only here
/cd ~/Projects/api wide   run here, but do not narrow the sandbox
/cd reset             unbind; the topic goes back to config.cwd
/cd                   what this topic is bound to, and how
```

| Sandbox mode | Writes inside the root | Writes outside the root |
|---|---|---|
| `read-only` | denied | denied |
| `workspace-write` | allowed | denied |
| `danger-full-access` | allowed | allowed |

`workspaceRoot` is the boundary, and it holds even when the turn switches its own
working directory: the refusal follows the configured root, not the directory the
agent moved to. That is the point — a model that wanders into another project
gets a refusal instead of a write.

Three things this table does **not** say, because measurement disagreed with the
obvious reading:

- the sandbox row alone changes nothing. `mode: read-only` in the
  `sandbox-policy` row plus `defaultPreset: danger-full-access` in the permission
  table still wrote outside the root. The permission table wins; the sandbox row
  is a default for a profile that has no table.
- `danger-full-access` therefore has to be chosen on purpose, per topic
  (`/permissions danger-full-access`), and it is the only mode that reaches
  outside the root.
- a preset with `approval: ask` cannot be used from a chat at all: a headless
  turn has no approval channel, so the escalation fails closed and the turn
  errors. `/permissions` lists such a preset with the reason instead of letting
  someone pick a trap.

Stock installs are not permission-enabled: `cordis.patch.yml` ships with the
`tg-bridge` plugin row only, so `/cd` binds the directory and `/permissions`
edits the profile-wide preset, exactly as before. The per-topic behaviour starts
the first time a profile gains a permission table.

### Goals and tasks

A topic carries its own goal and checklist, so the aim survives `/new`, a
restart and a different session:

```
/goal ship the release      set or replace the goal
/goal                       show the goal and the checklist
/tasks write the migration   add a task
/tasks done 2                tick it off
/tasks edit 2 shorter words   rewrite it in place, same number
/tasks rm 2                  remove it
/goal reopen                open a closed goal again
/goal done                  close the goal (all tasks done)
/goal clear                 delete the goal and its tasks
```

The bridge prepends the goal and the list to every turn, with the exact command
that updates it (`goal.mjs`). The agent ticks tasks as it finishes them, and the
next turn sees the new state. The bridge is the only writer of `state.json`: the
agent drops a job file into `goal-jobs/` and the bridge applies it, so there is
no lock race and no lost update.

## Security

- `config.json`, `state.json`, `pending/`, logs are in `.gitignore` and never
  end up in the repository.
- The token is stored in the DSH credentials store, not in code or config.
- The bridge only replies to ids in `allowedUserIds`.

## Documentation

- [docs/COMMANDS.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/COMMANDS.md): every command with what it does, in English, Russian and Chinese — the page `/help` links to
- [docs/LAYOUT.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/LAYOUT.md): which folder answers which question, and why the entry points stay at the root
- [docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md): BotFather settings, group and bot permissions
- [docs/SUPPORT.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/SUPPORT.md): what to send with a bug report, what never to send, and the one-line answer for "the bot went silent"
- [docs/VOICE.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/VOICE.md): any speech engine as input — a local script, a command with placeholders, an [OI]-compatible API
- [docs/MOBILE-FIRST.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/MOBILE-FIRST.md): working from a phone: what the chat shows, what it answers first, what it never makes you type
- [docs/COST.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/COST.md): what one turn costs and how to reduce it
- [docs/INJECTION-AND-REPLIES.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/INJECTION-AND-REPLIES.md): sending text into a turn that is still running, and how a reply is composed from its parts
- [docs/DEV-LOOP.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/DEV-LOOP.md): how work continues without a person at the keyboard — schedules, the queue, what a turn does when nobody watches
- [docs/REFACTORING.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/REFACTORING.md): moving code without ever shipping a broken version
- [docs/ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/ROADMAP.md): what comes next
- [docs/ONBOARDING-PLAN.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/ONBOARDING-PLAN.md): how a newcomer gets from "I found this repo" to a working bot
- [docs/UX-ANALYSIS.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/UX-ANALYSIS.md): interactive UX review
- [docs/HERMES-PARITY.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/HERMES-PARITY.md): DSH against the Hermes agent — what parity would take
- [docs/MARKETPLACE.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/MARKETPLACE.md): publishing in the DSH marketplace
- [docs/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/CHANGELOG.md): change history
- [docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md): release readiness criteria

2119143833877954569.title: dsh-find-plugins
2119143833877954569.desc: 跨多个社区目录并叠加 GitHub 与 npm 实时搜索来找 DSH 插件，按相关度、可信度、新鲜度与有界热度排序，而不是只看 star。
2119143833877954569.content:
# dsh-find-plugins

给 DeepSeek Harness **找到对的那个**插件，而不是找到一堆插件。

**中文** | [English](https://github.com/Eray114514/dsh-find-plugins/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

本插件给 agent 一个工具 —— `find_dsh_plugins` —— 搜遍整个 DSH 插件生态，
并按 **相关度 × 可信度 × 新鲜度 × 热度** 排序，而不是只看 star。

---

## 为什么要有它

两种显而易见的做法都有可以量化的毛病。

**只取 GitHub 一页再按 star 排**，会让一个名字里恰好带关键词的大仓库压掉真正的插件。
搜 `memory` 返回 8 个通用 agent 库、**0 个 DSH 插件**；搜 `terminal` 第 1 名是一个终端
**coding agent**，不是插件。

**只按字面名字匹配**，会让一个名字里不含关键词的知名插件沉底。实测一个 ★3k 的终端 UI
插件在搜 `terminal` 时排到 **第 117 位**，前面全是一排 ★1 仓库。

本插件的做法是聚合多个目录、按各自隐含的审查强度加权，并且把热度保留为一个**有界**信号
而不是全部答案：

| 查询 | 本工具 | GitHub 单页 + star | 字面名字匹配 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terminal` | `dsh-tianshu-tui` ★277 第 1（radar 实测 + 4 目录互证），`DSH-better-sidebar` ★3604 靠前 | 终端 coding agent 第 1 | 全是 ★1–★20 冷门仓库 |
| `memory` | `graph-memory` ★622、`MindMemOS` ★985、`dsh-mnemon` ★374 | 只有通用 agent 库 | `graph-memory` 第 1 |

---

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add dsh-find-plugins
```

然后重启 DSH。agent 就多了一个工具 `find_dsh_plugins`。

需要 DSH 0.1.5-rc.2 起、0.3.0 之前（含预发布）与 Node ≥ 22。范围写在 manifest 的 `engines.dsh`
里，`dsh plugin` 会在安装前核对，对不上时直接报出准确范围；当前桌面版 `0.2.1-rc.2` 是已实测的版本。

> `dsh-tools` 提供 `tools` 服务，**必须与宿主共享同一个实例**，所以走 `peerDependencies`
> 而不是 `dependencies` —— 后者会让 profile 里出现一份副本，覆盖运行时版本、导致服务激活失败。

---

## agent 会看到什么

```
本次查询了 7 个源：dsh.so ✓(11322 条) · radar ✓(280 条) · 岚叔目录 ✓(558 条) · awesome-dsh-plugin ✓(3722 条) · npm ✓(50 条 · 相关 4980) · dsh.works ✓(13056 条) · GitHub topic ✓(34 条 · 相关 43)
候选池 16368 条，命中 1185 条，返回 8 条。
（还有 1177 条命中未返回：需要更多就把 limit 调大，上限 20。）

1. huiliyi37/dsh-tianshu-tui  ★276  更新于 2026-09-14
   用途：DeepSeek Harness 的终端 UI（TUI）。
   装它：@huiliyi37/dsh-tianshu-tui
   npm 版本：1.0.0-rc.1（仓库已核对）
   可信：radar + 岚叔目录 + awesome-dsh-plugin + dsh.works · 实测过
   兼容：核对于 dsh 0.1.0-rc.8（2026-08-20）
```

这段输出里有六处比看起来更重要：

- **源状态头** —— 让 agent 能区分「生态里就这些」和「有一个目录超时了」；`相关 N` 只在源自己报了
  匹配总数时出现（搜索类源读的永远是一页，不是全部）；npm 源的长查询按 64 字符上限截断，被截断时
  状态里标 `查询已截断`，免得把「查窄了」读成「只有这些」；
- **`可信`** —— 哪些目录认识它、验证等级、安全扫描结果；
- **`风险`** —— 各目录自己的审查结论，包括「发现安装生命周期脚本」这类东西；
- **`兼容`** —— 目录是拿哪个 dsh 版本核对过的。兼容性是这生态第一失败模式（核心一次发版就可能砍掉
  某个 client 模块入口），所以源报了就一定呈现；工具同时探测**你正在运行的宿主版本**（探测不到就
  只报原始数字、不猜），核对版本与宿主**不同版本线**时标 ⚠，同线/一致也给出对照；
- **`⚠ 已 N 天未更新`** —— 超过 2 周没动静会在输出里点名，并在排序里**降权 15%**（乘法式，
  不打乱陈旧条目之间的相对次序）；日期未知不误报——没有日期不是废弃的证据；
- **`npm 版本`** —— 装它这一行给的是 npm 包时，附上 registry 里的版本；`（仓库已核对）` 表示拉过
  manifest 确认过 repository 字段指向同一个仓库。

---

## 怎么工作的

**数据源**（全部只读、实时拉取、进程内缓存）：

| 源 | 规模 | 提供什么 |
|---|---|---|
| dsh.so 索引 | ~15k | 验证等级 L1–L5、安全扫描、仓库健康度 |
| dsh.works 注册表 | ~13.5k | 每条都能指出安装路径的证据文件、核对时用的 dsh 版本、17 个功能标签、monorepo 子目录 |
| dsh-plugin-radar | ~280 | 唯一会**真的跑一遍**它收录的插件的目录 |
| awesome-dsh-plugin | ~3.6k | 人工双语描述、npm 包名 |
| 岚叔目录 | ~560 | 归档状态、最后提交时间、许可证、审查结论 |
| npm registry 搜索 | 实时(同类包 ~5k) | 只有它能看到"只发在 npm、没进任何目录、连仓库字段都没有"的包 |
| GitHub `dsh-plugin` / `dsh-plugins` topic | 实时 | 唯一能看到「今天刚发布」的源 |

挂掉的源只汇报自己的状态、不贡献内容；**拉取成功过、之后才失败**的源会回落到进程内缓存
副本并标注出来。**不落盘**，所以不会悄悄过期。

**安装目标（`装它` 那一行）**

- 源给的 npm 名优先；没有 npm 名时给 `github:owner/repo`；
- **源钉住的版本 ref 会保留**：目录发布的是 `github:o/r#v0.3.90`，就给 `#v0.3.90`，而不是退回
  `github:o/r` 去装"现在的 HEAD"——目录验证过的是那个版本；
- monorepo 里的包带 `#path:/<子目录>`（与 `#ref` 同时存在时用 `&` 连接）；
- 返回的每一行（≤20）会再拉一次 npm manifest 做校验：**manifest 声明了 `dsh`** 且
  `repository` 与条目仓库一致时，安装目标升级成 npm 包并附版本（npm tarball 是作者带着构建
  产物发布的；`github:` 安装不跑构建，仓库没提交 lib/ 的插件装出来就是缺文件的）。
  只有 npm 来源、且 manifest 里没有 `dsh` 的条目会被剔除并计数（关键字是自报的，不能当证据）。

**排序**

```
最终 = 相关度 × 可信度 × 新鲜度 × 热度
```

- **相关度** —— BM25，检索字段含 name / repo / npm 名 / 中英描述 / 分类 / topics。
  中文按**二字切分**，所以 `跨会话记忆` 能命中写着 `跨会话长期记忆` 的描述。
  原始分做了幂次压缩（0.45），否则乘数根本没机会影响排序。
- **可信度** —— 多源互相印证、dsh.so 验证等级、radar 实测过、安全风险、归档状态。
  **没有任何 DSH 专属目录认识它**的条目会被打折：dsh.so 也索引通用 agent 项目。
  npm 不算 DSH 专属证据——它的关键字是自报的。
- **新鲜度** —— 按最后提交时间衰减。**时间未知给中性分而不是零**：只有部分源提供时间，
  把「未知」当「已废弃」会把生态里大部分条目直接删掉。
- **热度** —— star 走**对数**，范围 0.6–1.3。★1 和 ★3000 只差约 1.5 倍。够用来偏向
  「有人在用」，不足以覆盖真实的相关度差距。

**风险等级是破平局用的，不是排除理由。** 自动化静态分析是弱信号，误报不该让一个好用的
插件掉队——何况装之前本来就该读源码。结论会**原样展示**在输出里，排序只轻轻推一下。

**查询**支持空格分隔的多个词，而且**更多词通常更好而不是更窄**——中英混排会让双语条目
的排序更准。几十组常见中英对照会自动扩展，**单复数也会双向折叠**（`screenshots` 与
`screenshot` 换出同一批候选——实测不折叠时一个命中 92 条、另一个只有 26 条且排名被换掉）；
只有调用方才知道的词（功能背后的服务名、用户没说出口的同义词）需要调用方补上。

**首调不等 20 秒**：目录类源是几 MB 的慢变数据，所以在插件加载后 5 秒起后台预热一次
（查询类源不预热——空查询不发请求）。冷启动实测从 ~20s 降到 ~3s。
`DSH_FIND_PLUGINS_NO_PREWARM=1` 可以彻底关掉预热。

**任何一次调用都有 25 秒的墙钟预算**：单个源的请求超时（最长 60s）约束不了整个调用，
所以超预算的源按 `timeout` 汇报（它的请求会继续跑并把结果留在缓存里，下一次是热的），
其余源照常返回。

---

## 边界

这些是刻意的，而且是有承重的：

- **只读。** 不装、不卸、不启停，绝不碰 profile 或 `cordis.patch.yml`。
- **不拥有索引。** 不内置快照、不写磁盘缓存。把过期数据当当前数据呈现，比没有数据更糟。
- **自己不做模型调用。** 调它的 agent 本身就是模型；再花一次调用去重排只会更慢更差。
- **完全不知道 dsh 外面套着什么桌面壳。** 本插件对任何 DSH 用户行为一致，这正是重点。

---

## 开发

```sh
npm install
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

**测试全部离线**（`globalThis.fetch` 被换成分派器，认不出的 URL 直接抛错，所以漏网的网络请求会
以失败的形式暴露），跑一遍不到 1 秒。fixtures 是**从各源真实抓取的样本**（`test/fixtures/`），
解析器是对着源**实际发出的格式**写的，不是对着它**应该发出的格式**。

### 可选：GitHub token

唯一用到凭据的地方是 GitHub 搜索源（其余目录都是公开 JSON，不需要认证）。
不带 token 时走匿名配额 **10 次/分钟**，正常使用足够（每次调用默认 2 个请求：单数/复数话题各一页）；
想放宽就设一个：

```sh
DSH_FIND_PLUGINS_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxx     # 或沿用通用的 GITHUB_TOKEN
```

只读公开数据，不需要任何 scope。

---

## 许可

MIT

2119143833877954568.title: dsh-perm-gate
2119143833877954568.desc: 已追加 cc-safety-net 风格的机械安全网规则，同时支持无模型、有模型辅助方式的安全审查，模式为自动审查、机械直通等。P0–P4 确定性优先权限门控，含 Permissive 档位、学习沉淀与审批历史 UI；凭据/受保护路径硬拒绝，内部只读工具自动放行。
2119143833877954568.content:
# dsh-perm-gate

- [English README](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/README.md)
- [中文 README](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/README.zh.md)
- [日本語 README](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/README.ja.md)
- [한국어 README](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/README.ko.md)
- [Installation guide](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/INSTALL.md)
- [中文安装指南](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/INSTALL.zh.md)
- [日本語インストールガイド](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/INSTALL.ja.md)
- [한국어 설치 안내](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/INSTALL.ko.md)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)
- [日本語 changelog](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.ja.md)
- [한국어 changelog](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.ko.md)

> **兼容性说明：** v2.0.0 自带 `ja` / `ko` 字典，但官方 DSH 的 `LocaleRuntime`
> 只暴露 `zh` / `en`（`LOCALE_IDS = ["zh", "en"]`）。在原版 DSH 上选择 `ja` / `ko`
> 会报 `locale "<id>" is not registered`。请使用更新了 `LOCALE_IDS`
> （locale-settings.ts）与 `LOCALES` 标签（client/index.ts）的 DSH fork 并重新构建。

> **▼ DSH 版本适配**
>
> 两个 DSH 版本线从两个长期分支分别维护，各有一套版本号系列、`engines.dsh`
> 和 npm 分发标签（[发布布局](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/RELEASING.md)）：
>
> | DSH 版本 | 分支 | 版本号 | npm 标签 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 0.1.0-rc.7 ~ 0.1.1-rc.x | `legacy` | `1.x` | `@legacy` |
> | 0.1.2-alpha.1+（含 0.1.5-rc.2） | `main` | `2.x` | `@latest` / `@dsh-0.1.2` （`@2.x` 是范围） |
>
> 版本序列号跟的是 **DSH 线**（`1.x` = DSH ≤ 0.1.1，`2.x` = DSH 0.1.2+），两条大版本互
> 相隔离：锁在 `^1.x` 的安装绝不会解析到 `2.x`，反之亦然。`engines.dsh` 表达同样的
> 分界，但 DSH 从不读取它——真正把旧 DSH 钉在 `1.x` 上的是版本范围与 dist-tag。
>
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` 在 `0.1.2-alpha.1` 中已被**移除**——不仅仅是更名。
> `legacy` 线仍通过它访问 `ctx.slots`；`main` 从
> `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer/client` 获得相同的声明。两处版本敏感
> 接缝通过**能力探测**处理，而非版本号检查：（1）设置注册使用 `register`，两线
> 都存在（`installSection` 是新增项，不是替代）；（2）`effectivePolicy` 在两
> 线上都是 user-approval 服务的**私有**方法，因此通过 `typeof` 探测读取，缺失
> 或抛错时降级为「策略未知」。

版本 **2.4.1** —— 变更见 [Changelog](https://github.com/drscrewdriver/dsh-perm-gate/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md)。

一个**单一自足、确定性优先、fail-closed** 的 DeepSeek Harness 权限门插件。

对每个工具调用按固定优先级链裁决：

| 阶段 | 决策 | 含义 |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| **P0** | `deny` | 确定性硬拒：凭据材料 / 受保护路径改写 / 危险 shell |
| **P1** | `allow` | 精确、有界的**会话放行** grant |
| **P2** | `deny/allow/ask` | 静态规则链：黑名单优先，其次 allow，再 ask |
| **P3** | `allow/deny/ask` | 可选 LLM 语义分类器（默认**关闭**） |
| **P4** | `ask` | 官方 approval seam |

严格 fail-closed：P0 永不因 grant / 规则 / 分类器 / 人工而放行。
